If $\underset{x\to a}{Lt}f(x)=\ell(\ne0)$ then prove that in a deleted neighbourhood of $a$, $f$ keeps the same sign as that of $\ell$.
Prove that every monotone decreasing sequence which is bounded below is convergent and converges to is greatest lower bound.
Prove that a sequence is convergent iff it is a Cauchy sequence.
Examine if the sequence $x_n=1-\frac12+\frac13+\text{----}+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}n$ is a Cauchy sequence.

Prove that every continuous function defined over a closed bounded interval $[a,b]$ is bounded there in and attains its bounds. Does the result hold if $[a,b]$ is replaced by an open interval $(a,b)$?
Verify the differentiability of the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}x\sin\frac1x&\text{for }x\ne0\\0&\text{for }x=0\end{cases}$ At $x=0$.
If $y=x^{2x}$, $n$ is a positive integer, then show that $y_n=2^n\{1.3.5.\text{---}(2n-1)\}x^n$.
Show that $\cosh x\ge1$ for all real $x$.
State and prove Libnitz's theorem for successive differentiation.
If $y=e^{a\sin^{-1}x}$ then show that $(1-x^2)y_{n+2}-(2n+1)xy_{n+1}-(n^2+a^2)y_n=0$ and hence find $(y_n)_0$.
Prove that a point $\xi$ is a limit point of a set $A$ iff every neighbourhood of $\xi$ contains infinitely many points of $A$.
Define a derived set. Show that derived set of a bounded set is bounded.
Let $S$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb R$ and $T$ be a set given by $T=\{x-y:x,y\in S\}$.\par Prove that (i) $Sup\,T=Sup\,S-Inf\,S$.\par (ii) $Inf\,T=Inf\,S-Sup\,S$.
From the relation $f(x+h)=f(x)+hf'(x+\theta h)$, show that $\theta$ is independent on $x$ where $f(x)=a+bx+cm^x$, where $a,b,c$ are constants.
If $n$ is an even positive integer then show that $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^nx\,dx=\frac{n-1}n\cdot\frac{n-3}{n-2}\cdot\frac{n-5}{n-4}\ldots\frac34\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac\pi2$
If $I_n=\int x^n\sqrt{a-x}\,dx$ then show that $(2n+3)I_n=2anI_{n-1}-2x^n(a-x)^{3/2}$ and hence evaluate $\int_0^ax^3\sqrt{ax-x^2}\,dx$

Prove by the principle of mathematical induction that for every positive integer $n$, $(\cos\theta_1+i\sin\theta_1)(\cos\theta_2+i\sin\theta_2)\ldots(\cos\theta_n+i\sin\theta_n)=\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2+\ldots+\theta_n)+i\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2+\ldots+\theta_n)$ Hence deduce De Moivre's theorem for positive integers.
Show that the mapping $f:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ defined by $f(x)=\frac x{1+|x|}$ is a bijective mapping. Also find $f^{-1}$.
Prove that for any positive integer $n$, $3n^2-1$ is never a perfect square.
Show that the product of four consecutive integers is $1$ less than a perfect square.
For positive integers $n$ and positive integers $a,b$ show that the relation $a^n\mid b^n$ implies that $a\mid b$.
If $p\ge q\ge5$ and $p$ and $q$ are both primes, then show that $24\mid p^2-q^2$.
Show that there are infinite number of primes. Give an example to show that there are arbitrarily large gaps in the sequence of primes.
Find the remainder when the sum $1^5+2^5+\text{---}+100^5$ is divided by $4$. Also by using Format's theorem find the unit digit of $3^{100}$.
Obtain three consecutive integers, each having factor $2^2$, $3^2$ and $5^2$, respectively.
Let $m,n$ be two positive integers. Show that $\varphi(m,n)=\frac{\varphi(m)\varphi(n)gcd(m,n)}{\varphi(\gcd(m,n))}$
If $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers, Also show that $m^{\varphi(n)}+n^{\varphi(m)}\equiv1(\mathrm{mod}\ mn)$
Determine if the following system of linear equations $x-2y+z=0$, $y-4z=4$ and $x-z=2$ is consistent. If so, find a solution.
Row reduce the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3&-6&4&9\\-1&-2&-1&3&1\\-2&-3&0&3&-1\\1&4&5&-9&-7\end{pmatrix}$ to echelon form and find the pivot columns of $A$.

Let $a_1=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\-5\end{pmatrix},\ a_2=\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\\6\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}7\\4\\-3\end{pmatrix}$. Determine whether $b$ is a linear combination of $a_1$ and $a_2$. Give geometric description of $L(\{a_1,a_2\})$.

Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ matrix. Show that the following conditions are equivalent:\par
i) for each $b\in\mathbb R^m$, the equation $AX=b$ has a solution.\par
ii) each $b\in\mathbb R^m$ is a linear combination of the columns of $A$.\par
iii) the columns of $A$ spans $\mathbb R^m$.
Describe all solutions of $Ax=b$, where $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&5&-4\\-3&-2&4\\6&1&-8\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}7\\1\\-4\end{pmatrix}$.

Define a linear transformation $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$. If $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is a linear transformation, then prove that $T$ is one-to-one if and only if the equation $T(X)=0,\ X\in\mathbb R^n$ has only the trivial solution.

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix. Prove that the following conditions are equivalent.\par
i) $A$ is an invertible matrix\par
ii) $A$ is row equivalent to the $n\times n$ identity matrix\par
iii) $A$ has $n$ pivot position\par
iv) the equation $Ax=0$ has only the trivial solution.
Define subspace of $\mathbb R^3$. Show that any plane through the origin is a subspace in $\mathbb R^3$.
Find the dimension of the null space of $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&4&-2&1\\-2&-5&7&3\\3&7&-8&6\end{pmatrix}$
Define eigen value and eigen vector of a matrix $A$. If $\lambda$ an eigen value of a non-singular matrix $A$, then show that $\lambda^{-1}$ is an eigen value of $A^{-1}$.
Show that two nonzero eigen vectors of a square matrix $A$ over $\mathbb R$ corresponding to two distinct eigen values are linearly independent.
The characteristic roots of a $3\times3$ real matrix $A$ are in A.P.. Determine the characteristic roots, where trace $A=15$ and $|A|=80$.
If $\lambda$ is an eigen value of a nonsingular matrix $A$, then show that $\frac{|A|}\lambda$ is an eigen value of adj $A$.
If $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\4&5\end{pmatrix}$. Find the eigen values and the eigen vectors of $A$.
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb R$. Show that to a non-zero eigen vector of $A$ there corresponds unique eigen value of $A$.
State completeness property of $\mathbb R$ and hence deduce that every nonempty subset of $\mathbb R$ which is bounded below has an intimum.
Find the `sup' and `$Inf$' of the set $\{x\in\mathbb R:3x^2+8x-3<0\}$.
State Archimedean property of $\mathbb R$. Prove that if $x\in\mathbb R$ and $x>0$, then $\exists$ a natural number $m$ such that $m-1\le x<m$.
State and prove Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem for a set.
Show that for any two subsets $A,B$ of $\mathbb R$, $(A\cap B)'\subset A'\cap B'$. Does the equality hold? Give reasons.
If $G\subset\mathbb R$ is an open set, then prove that $\mathbb R\setminus G$ is closed set.
Let $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}0&\text{if }x\in[-1,0]\\1&\text{if }x\in(0,1]\end{cases}$ Does there exist a function $g$ such that $g'(x)=f(x)\ \forall x\in[-1,1]$ ?
State and prove Lagrange's MVT. Give its geometrical interpretation.
Show that between any two real roots of $e^x\cos x+1=0$ there is at least one real root of the equation $e^x\sin x+1=0$.
Find the asymptotes of the curve $x^3+x^2y-xy^2-y^3+x^2-y^2=2$.
Find the points of inflexion, if any, of the curve $y=x^3$.
If $\underset{x\to a}{Lt}f(x)=\ell$ and $\underset{x\to a}{Lt}g(x)=m$ then prove that $\underset{x\to a}{Lt}f(x)g(x)=\ell m$.
Let $f:[a,b]\to[c,d]$ and $g:[c,d]\to[e,f]$ be two continuous mappings. Prove that $g\circ f:[a,b]\to[e,f]$ is continuous.
If a sequence $\{x_n\}$ converges to $\ell$ then show that the sequence $\{y_n\}$ where $y_n=\frac{x_1+x_2+\ldots+x_n}n$ converges to $\ell$.
Prove that every Cauchy sequence of real numbers is bounded.
Examine if the sequence $\{x_n\}$ where $x_n=1+\frac12+\frac13+\ldots+\frac1n$ is a Cauchy sequence.

Let $\{[a_n,b_n]\}$ be a sequence of closed bounded intervals of $\mathbb R$ such that $[a_{n+1},b_{n+1}]\subset[a_n,b_n]$ for $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ and $b_n-a_n\to0$ as $n\to\infty$. Prove that $\exists$ unique $\ell$ such that $\ell\in[a_n,b_n]\ \forall n=1,2,3,\ldots..$
Prove that the sequence $\{x_n\}$ defined by $x_1=\sqrt7$ and $x_{n+1}=\sqrt{7+x_n}$ for all $n\ge1$ converges to the positive root of the equation $x^2-x-7=0$.
Obtain a reduction formula for $\int\cos^mx\sin nx\,dx$ and deduce the value of $\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^5x\sin3x\,dx$..
State L. Hospital's theorem and evaluate $\underset{x\to0}{Lt}\left(\frac{\sin x}x\right)^{1/x}$.
Draw the column picture for the solution of the system of equations $x+y=5,\ x-y=-1$.

Show that the following system of equations is inconsistent.\par
$y-4z=8$,\quad $2x-3y+2z=1$,\quad $4x-8y+12z=1$
Find an equation involving $g,h,k$ that makes the following augmented matrix corresponds to a consistent system $\begin{pmatrix}1&-4&7&g\\0&3&-5&h\\-2&5&-9&k\end{pmatrix}$.

Find the reduced row echelon form of $\begin{pmatrix}0&3&-6&6&4&-5\\3&-7&8&-5&8&9\\3&-9&12&-9&6&15\end{pmatrix}$. Hence or otherwise list the free and basic variables of the corresponding system of equations. Also find its solution.
Suppose the coefficient matrix of a system of linear equations has a pivot position in every row. Explain why the system is consistent.
Find the equation to describe geometrically, span $(\{(1,2,1),(2,-3,0)\})$.
Express $b=(7,4,-3)$ as a linear combination of $a_1=(1,-2,-5)$ and $a_2=(2,5,6)$.
Suppose $A$ is a $3\times3$ matrix and $b$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with the property that $Ax=b$ has a unique solutions. Explain why the columns of $A$ must span $\mathbb R^3$.
Examine if the columns of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-8&5\\3&-7&4\\-1&5&-4\\1&-3&2\end{pmatrix}$ are linearly independent.
Prove that a set of vectors $S=\{v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_p\}$ in $\mathbb R^n$ is linearly dependent if and only if at least one of the vectors is $S$ is a linear combination of the others.
Suppose that an $m\times n$ matrix $A$ has $n$ pivot columns. Explain why for each $b$ in $\mathbb R^m$ the system $Ax=b$ has at most one solution.
Find the linear transformation $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ which represents the following two consecutive reflections.

Let $T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be a linear transformation given by $T(e_1)=(2,-3,1)$, $T(e_2)=(0,-2,5)$ and $T(e_3)=(-1,3,4)$. Find $T(x,y,z)$, where $e_1,e_2$ and $e_3$ are the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb R^3$. Hence find the standard matrix of $T$.

Let $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be a linear transformation and $A$ be the standard matrix of $T$. Prove that $T$ maps $\mathbb R^n$ onto $\mathbb R^m$ if and only if the columns of $A$ spans $\mathbb R^m$.
Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ matrix. If $A$ is invertible, then show that the linear transformation $x\to Ax$ is one-to-one.
Find a basis for the null space of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}-3&6&1&1&-7\\1&-2&2&3&-1\\2&-4&5&8&-4\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be a linear transformation. Show that $\ker T$ is a subspace of $\mathbb R^n$.
What can you say about null $B$, when $B$ is a $5\times4$ matrix with linearly independent columns.
Determine the rank of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&5&-3&-4&8\\4&7&-4&-3&9\\6&9&-5&2&4\\0&-9&6&5&-6\end{pmatrix}$
Find a basis and the dimension of $W$ where $W=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3\mid x+2y+3z=0\}$
Find the eigen values of $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&-1&6\\2&1&6\\2&-1&8\end{pmatrix}$. Also find the eigen space corresponding to the repeated eigen value, if any.
Construct an example of a $2\times2$ matrix which has only one eigen value.

Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be two non zero complex numbers. If $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be arguments of $z_1$ and $z_2$ respectively, then show that $\theta_1+\theta_2$ is an argument of $z_1z_2$.\par
Does the result hold it one considers the principal arguments of complex numbers? Justify your answer.

If $n$ is a positive integer and $(1+z)^n=a_0+a_1z+\ldots+a_nz^n$, then prove that\par
(i) $a_0-a_2+a_4-\ldots=2^{n/2}\cos\frac{n\pi}4$\par
(ii) $a_1-a_3+a_5-\ldots=2^{n/2}\sin\frac{n\pi}4$
Show that the product of all values of $(\sqrt3+i)^{3/5}$ is $8i$.
Let $a,b,c,d$ be four positive real numbers, not all equal. Then show that the equation $(x-a)^3+(x-b)^3+(x-c)^3+(x-d)^3=0$ has only one real root.

If $\alpha,\beta$ and $\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $2x^3+x^2+x+1=0$, find the equation whose roots are $\frac1{\alpha^2}+\frac1{\beta^2}-\frac1{\gamma^2},\ \frac1{\alpha^2}-\frac1{\beta^2}+\frac1{\gamma^2},\ -\frac1{\alpha^2}+\frac1{\beta^2}+\frac1{\gamma^2}$. Hence find the value of $\frac1{\alpha^2}+\frac1{\beta^2}+\frac1{\gamma^2}$.
Expand $f(x)=x^4-x^3+2x^2+6x-2$ as a polynomial in $x-2$ and then find $f(x+2)$
If $x,y,z$ are positive real numbers and $x+y+z=1$, prove that $8xyz\le(1-x)(1-y)(1-z)\le\frac8{27}$.
Express $f(x)=x^4-2x^3-5x^2+10x-3$ in the form $(x^2+px+q)^2-(ax+b)^2$ and hence, solve the equation $f(x)=0$.
Find the angle through which the axes are to be rotated so that the equation $7x^2+8xy-5y^2=1$ may be reduced to the form $Ax^2+By^2=1,\ A>0$; find also $A$ and $B$.
Verify whether the equation of the pair of straight lines through the origin perpendicular to the pair of straight lines $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ is $bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0$.
Derive the equations of the tangents to the conic $x^2+4xy+3y^2-5x-6y+3=0$ which are parallel to the straight line $x+4y=-2$, if exists.
Find the pole of the straight line $2x-5y=4$ with respect to the parabola $y^2=8x$.
Reduce the equation $6x^2-5xy-4y^2+7x+8y+4=0$ to its canonical form and determine the nature of the conic.

Show that the straight line $r\cos(\theta-\beta)=p$ in polar coordinate touches the conic $\frac lr=1+e\cos\theta$, if $(l\cos\beta-ep)^2+l^2\sin^2\beta=p^2$. 
\begin{center}\textbf{Gr.-B} (Full Marks=24)\\(Three Dimensional Geometry)\\Answer \textit{any three} questions.\end{center}
Find the angle between two straight lines whose directions cosines are given by $l+m+n=0$, $l^2+m^2-n^2=0$, if they are not parallel.
Verify whether the equation $2x^2-y^2+3z^2-xy+7xz+2yz=0$ represents a pair of planes. Find the angle between them, if yes and are not parallel.

A plane cuts the coordinate axes in $A,B,C$ such that the centroid of the triangle $ABC$ is the point $(a,b,c)$. Show that the equation of the plane is $\frac xa+\frac yb+\frac zc=k$, where $k$ is a number to be determined by you.
Prove that the plane passing through the point $(a,b,c)$ containing the straight line $x=py+q=rz+s$ can be put into the form $\begin{vmatrix}x&py+q&rz+s\\a&pb+q&rc+s\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=0$.
Show that by a special choice of coordinate axes the equation of two skew lines can be put in the form $y=\pm mx,\ z=c$.
Obtain the equation of the sphere through the point $(1,1,2)$ and $(2,-2,3)$ and having its center on the line $2x+3y=0=5x+y-z$.

Prove that a general equation of second degree $ax^2+by^2+cz^2+2fyz+2gzx+2hxy+2ux+2vy+2wz+d=0$ may represent a cone provided the condition $\begin{vmatrix}a&h&g&u\\h&b&f&v\\g&f&c&w\\u&v&w&d\end{vmatrix}=0$ on coefficients $a,b,c,f,g,h,u,v,w,d$ holds.
Derive the equation of a cylinder whose guiding curve is $ax^2+by^2+2hxy+2gx+2fy+c=0,\ z=0$ and whose generators are parallel to the line $\frac xl=\frac ym=\frac zn$.
Let $S$ be a non-empty bounded subset of $\mathbb R$ with $\sup S=M$ and $Inf\,S=m$. Find $\sup T$ and $Inf\,T$ where $T=\{x-y:x,\ y\in S\}$.
Let $x,y\in\mathbb R$ and $x<y$. Then prove that\par i) there is a rational number $r$ such that $x<r<y$.\par ii) there is an irrational number $s$ such that $x<s<y$.
If $a\in\mathbb R$ and $0\le a<\frac1n$ for every natural number $n$, then prove that $a=0$.
Show that a finite set has no limit points.
Give an example of an infinite set $S\subset\mathbb R$ such that $S$ has no limit points.
Show that for any two subsets, $A,B$ of $\mathbb R$, $(A\cup B)'=A'\cup B'$.
Find the derived set of the set $S=\{\frac1n:n\in\mathbb N\}$.
State and prove Rollel's theorem. Give its geometrical interpretations.
Prove that between any two real roots of the equation $e^x\sin x+1=0$, there is at least one real root of the equation $\tan x+1=0$.
Let $f$ be a real valued function defined on $\mathbb R$ satisfying $|f(x)-f(y)|\le(x-y)^2\quad\forall x,y\in\mathbb R$. Prove that $f$ is constant on $\mathbb R$.
State Leibnitz theorem for higher order derivatives. If $y=e^{a\sin^{-1}x}$, prove that $(1-x^2)y_{n+2}-(2n+1)xy_{n+1}-(n^2+a^2)y_n=0$.
If $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$, then prove that $f'([a,b])$ is an interval.
Let a function $f$ be twice differentiable on $[a,b]$ and $f(a)=f(b)=0$ and $f(a)<0$ for some $c\in(a,b)$. Prove that there is at least one point $\xi\in(a,b)$ for which $f''(\xi)>0$.
State sequential criterion for limit and use it to show that $\lim_{x\to0}\tan\frac1x$ does not exist.
Prove that every monotone decreasing sequence which is bounded below is convergent and converges to its greatest lower bound.
Let $\{x_n\}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{x_{n+1}}{x_n}\right)=\ell$. Then prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}x_n^{1/n}=\ell$.
Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous such that for $c\in(a,b),\ f(c)\ne0$. Show that $\exists\delta>0$ such that $f(x)$ has the same sign as that of $f(c)\ \forall x\in(c-d,c+d)\cap[a,b]$.
A function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\ \forall x,y\in\mathbb R$. If $f(1)=k$, prove that $f(x)=kx\ \forall x\in\mathbb R$.
Find the points of discontinuity of the function $f$ where $f(x)=[x]+[-x],\ x\in\mathbb R$.
If $n$ is an odd positive integer then show that $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^nx\,dx=\frac{n-1}n\cdot\frac{n-3}{n-2}\cdot\frac{n-5}{n-4}\ldots\frac45\cdot\frac28\cdot1$.
State L. Hospital's theorem and hence evaluate $\lim_{x\to0}\left(\frac{\tan x}x\right)^{1/x}$.

Find the general solution of the system of equations whose augmented matrix is given by $\begin{pmatrix}1&-7&0&6&5\\0&0&1&-2&-3\\-1&7&-4&2&7\end{pmatrix}$. \par
Explain the consistency of a system of linear equations whose coefficient matrix has a pivot position in every rows.
Give an example to show that row echelon form of a matrix may not be unique.
Let $m,n,p$ be three positive integers such that $m>n$. Suppose that $A$ and $B$ be two matrices of order $m\times n$ and $n\times p$ respectively. If row rank of $B$ is $p$, find row rank of $AB$.

Suppose $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)$ be such that $C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_n$ are $n$ columns of $A$. If the system of equations $AX=b$ has a solution show that $b$ is a linear combination of $C_1,C_2,\ldots,C_n$.
Give a geometric description of span $(\{(8,2,-6),(12,13,-9)\})$.

Given $A$ be a $3\times4$ matrix, let $y_1$ and $y_2$ be two vectors in $\mathbb R^3$, and let $w=y_1+y_2$. Suppose $y_1=Ax_1$ and $y=Ax_2$ for some vectors $x_1,x_2$ in $\mathbb R^4$. Find the condition such that the system $Ax=w$ is consistent?

Suppose that the solution set of a certain system of linear equations can be described as $x_1=5+4x_3,\ x_2=-2-7x_3$, with $x_3$ free. Use these vectors to describe that this set represents a line in $\mathbb R^3$.
Show that two vectors in $\mathbb R^2$ is linearly dependent if and only if they lie on a line passing through the origin.
How many pivot columns must be in a $5\times7$ matrix, if its columns span $\mathbb R^5$? Justify your answer.
Determine if the columns of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&4&-3&0\\-2&-7&5&1\\-4&-5&7&5\end{pmatrix}$ forms a linearly independent set in $\mathbb R^3$.
Let $H$ be the set of points inside and on the unit circle in the $xy$-plane. Show that $H$ is not a subspace of $\mathbb R^3$.

Find a basis and dimension of the null space of $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-3&2&-4\\-3&9&-1&5\\2&-6&4&-3\\-4&12&2&7\end{pmatrix}$ in $\mathbb R^4$. Hence find the dimension of column space of $A$, by using Rank-Nullity Theorem.
How the linear independenceness of the row vectors of a square matrix depend on its nonsingularity?
Let $T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2$ be defined by, $T(x,y,z)=(x-y+z,\ 2x+y-3z)$. Show that $T$ is a linear transformation. Interpret Ker $T$ geometrically.

Let $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be a linear transformation, and let $\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}$ be a linearly dependent set in $\mathbb R^n$. Explain whether the set $\{Tv_1,Tv_2,Tv_3\}$ is linearly independent or not.

Let $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be a linear transformation that maps $u=\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}$ into $\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}$ and maps $v=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\end{pmatrix}$ into $\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\end{pmatrix}$. Find the image of $3u+2v$.

If $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ are eigen vectors that correspond to distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\text{---},\lambda_n$ of an $n\times n$ matrix $A$, then show that the set $\{v_1,v_2,\text{---},v_n\}$ is linearly independent.
Consider an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ with the property that the row sums are all equal and equals to $s$. Show that $s$ is an eigen value of $A$.

Find a basis for the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda=4$ of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}3&0&2&0\\1&3&1&0\\0&1&1&0\\0&0&0&4\end{pmatrix}$. Hence find the dimension of column space of $A-4I$, where $I$ is the $4\times4$ identity matrix.
If $\alpha=\cos\frac{2\pi}n+i\sin\frac{2\pi}n$ and $p$ is prime to n, then prove that $1+\alpha^p+\alpha^{2p}+\ldots+\alpha^{(n-1)p}=0$.
If $n$ be a positive integer and $(1+z)^n=p_0+p_1z+p_2z^2+\ldots+p_nz^n$, prove that $p_0+p_4+p_8+\ldots=2^{n-2}+2^{(n-2)/2}\cos\frac{n\pi}4.$.
Show that the sum of the 99th powers of the roots of the equation $z^7-1=0$ is zero.
State Fundamental Theorem of Classical Algebra. Show that an mth degree algebraic equation has exactly $m$ number of roots.
Show that the equation $(x-a)^3+(x-b)^3+(x-c)^3+(x-d)^3=0$, where $a,b,c,d$ are all positive and not all equal, has only one real root.
If $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $x^3+px^2+qx+r=0$, find the value of $(\beta+\gamma-\alpha)^3+(\gamma+\alpha-\beta)^3+(\alpha+\beta-\gamma)^3$.

If $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $x^3-2x^2+3x-1=0$, find the value of $\frac{\beta\gamma-\alpha^2}{\beta+\gamma-2\alpha},\ \frac{\gamma\alpha-\beta^2}{\gamma+\alpha-2\beta},\ \frac{\alpha\beta-\gamma^2}{\alpha+\beta-2\gamma}$.
If $a,b,c$ are sides of a triangle and $a+b+c=2s$, then show that\par i) $s^3\ge27(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$\par ii) $\frac{s^2}{3\sqrt3}\ge A$, where $A=$ area of the triangle.
Let $S$ be a bounded subset of $\mathbb R$ with $SupS=M$ and $InfS=m$. Prove that the set $T=\{x-y:x\in S,y\in S\}$ is a bounded set with $SupT=M-m$ and $InfT=m-M$.
Prove that $\mathbb N$ is unbounded above.
Is $\mathbb Q$ dense in $\mathbb R$? Justify your answer.
For any $A,B\subset\mathbb R$, prove that $(A\cap B)'\subset A'\cap B'$. Is the converse true? Justify .
If $f'$ exist in $[0,1]$, show that the equation $2x(f(1)-f(0))=f'(x)$ has atleast one solution in $(0,1)$.
If $f'(x)\ge0$ on $[1,2]$, then prove that $f\left(\frac{x+y}2\right)\le\frac{f(x)+f(y)}2$, $\forall x,y\in[1,2]$ .
By using $(\epsilon-\delta)$ definition, evaluate $\lim_{x\to2}\frac{2x^2-8}{x-2}$ and find $\delta$ if $\epsilon=0.1$.
If $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=l$ and $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)=m\ne0$ then prove that $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\frac lm$.
Examine the continuity of the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{x^4+4x^3+2x}{\sin x}&\text{when }x\ne0\\0&\text{when }x=0\end{cases}$ at $x=0$.
Let $f:[a,b]\to[c,d]$ and $g:[c,d]\to[e,f]$ be two continuous mappings. Prove that $g\circ f:[a,b]\to[e,f]$ is continuous.
A function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfies the condition $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ $\forall x,y\in\mathbb R$. If $f$ is continuous at $x=0$, prove that $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$.
State and prove nested intervals theorem.
Find the limit of the sequence $\{x_n\}$ where $x_n=(2^n+3^n)^{1/n}$.
Prove that a sequence is convergent iff it is a Cauchy sequence.
Give an example of a sequence of rational numbers that converges to an irrational number.
Define zero of a polynomial. Find the multiple root(s) of the polynomial $x^4-9x^2+4x+12=0$ and solve the equation.
State and prove the factor theorem.
If $x^2+px+1$ is a factor of the polynomial $ax^3+bx+c$, then show that $a^2-c^2=ab$.
Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4$ be the four roots of the equation $x^4+p_1x^3+p_2x^2+p_3x+p_4=0$. Find the value of $(1+a_1^2)(1+a_2^2)(1+a_3^2)(1+a_4^2)$.
State the Descarte's rule of signs. Using the Descarte's rule of signs, show that the equation $x^7+5x^4-3x+k=0$ can have at most three real roots for every real number $k$.
Form a biquadratic equation with real coefficients two of whose roots are given by $3i\pm5$.

Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be three roots of the equation $x^3+qx+r=0$. Find the equation whose roots are $\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+1,\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma+1,\frac1\gamma+\frac1\alpha+1$. Hence or otherwise find the value of $(\alpha+\beta+\alpha\beta)(\beta+\gamma+\beta\gamma)(\gamma+\alpha+\gamma\alpha)$.
Reduce the cubic equation $8x^3-36x^2+42x-5=0$ to its standard form and then solve by the Cardan's method.
Show that every matrix is row equivalent to a unique matrix in reduced row echelon form.

Find an equation involving $g,h$ and $k$ that makes the augmented matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&-4&7&g\\0&3&-5&h\\-2&5&-9&k\end{pmatrix}$ correspond to a consistent system. Hence or otherwise find $span((1,0,-2),(-4,3,5),(7,-5,-9))$.
Suppose the coefficient matrix of a system of linear equations has a pivot position in every row. Explain why the system is consistent. Find with justification if the system has unique solution.
Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ matrix. Prove that the system $Ax=b$ has a solution for every $b\in\mathbb R^m$ if and only if $r(A)=m$.
Let $v_1=(3,0,2)$ and $v_2=(2,0,3)$. Give a geometric description of $span(v_1,v_2)$ without finding it explicitly.
Let $v_1,v_2,\cdots,v_m$ be $m$ vectors in $\mathbb R^n$. Prove that they are linearly dependent if and only if either of them is a linear combination of the others.
Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix with the property that the system $AX=b$ has unique solution for some $b\in\mathbb R^3$. Explain why the columns of $A$ span $\mathbb R^3$.
Show that every subspace of $\mathbb R^n$ has a basis.
Find the row space of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2&3\\5&-4&3\\9&-3&-3\end{pmatrix}$. Show that the solution space of $AX=0$ is orthogonal to the row space.
Prove that the pivot columns of $A$ form a basis of the column space $C(A)$.
Suppose that $\mathbb R^3=span(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$. Explain why $\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}$ is a basis of $\mathbb R^3$.
Show that a non null proper subspace of $\mathbb R^3$ is either a line through the origin or a plane through the origin.
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix. Prove that the columns of $A$ form a basis of $\mathbb R^n$ if and only if $A$ is invertible.
Find the eigen values of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-2&-3\\-1&1&-1\\2&2&5\end{pmatrix}$ and the eigen vectors belonging to some one of the eigen values.
Let $A$ be a square matrix such that $A^2=0$. Show that $0$ is the only eigen value of $A$.

If $I_{m,n}=\int\cos^mx\cos nx\,dx$, show that $$I_{m,n}=\frac{\cos^mx\sin nx}{m+n}+\frac m{m+n}I_{m-1,n-1}=\frac{n\sin nx\cos x-m\cos nx\sin x}{n^2-m^2}\cos^{m-1}x-\frac{m(m-1)}{n^2-m^2}I_{m-2,n}.$$ Hence deduce that $\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^nx\cos nx\,dx=\frac\pi{2^{n+1}}$.

Examine whether the improper integral $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{\sin x}$ exists. If so, find its value.

Prove that the entire area of the loop of the curve, given by, $(ax)^{2/3}+(by)^{2/3}=(a^2-b^2)$ is $\frac{3\pi}8\frac{(a^2-b^2)^2}{ab}$.

Give $(\epsilon-\delta)$ definition of the limit of a function and hence evaluate $\lim_{x\to5}f(x)$ where $f(x)=x^3+3x-10$, $x\in[4,10]$. Find $\delta$ if $\epsilon=0.5$.
If $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=l$ and $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)=m$, then prove that $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)g(x)=lm$.
Prove that a function $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous iff for any $c\in[a,b]$ and for any sequence $\{x_n\}\in[a,b]$ converging to $c$, $\{f(x_n)\}$ converges to $f(c)$.
If a sequence $\{x_n\}$ converges to $l$ then prove that the sequence $\{y_n\}$ where $y_n=\frac{x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n}n$ converges to $l$.
Define Cauchy sequence and give an example for the same. Prove that every Cauchy sequence is bounded. Does the converse hold? Justify.
Examine if the sequence $x_n=1-\frac12+\frac13+\cdots+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}n$ is a Cauchy sequence.
State and Prove Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem.
From the relation $f(x+h)=f(x)+hf'(x+\theta h)$, show that $\theta$ is independent on $x$ for $f(x)=a+bx+cm^x$ where $a,b,c,m$ are constants.
If $f'(x)=0$ for all values of $x$ in an interval then prove that $f(x)$ is constant in that interval.
Let $S$ be a non-empty bounded subset of $\mathbb R$ with $supS=M$ and $infS=m$. Find $SupT$ and $InfT$ where $T=\{x-y:x\in S,y\in S\}$.
Let $x,y\in\mathbb R$ and $x<y$. Then prove that\\(i) there is a rational number $r$ such that $x<r<y$.\\(ii) there is an irrational number $s$ such that $x<s<y$.
Find the values of $a,b,c$ so that $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{(a+b\cos x)x-c\sin x}{x^5}=1$.
Obtain a reduction formula for $\int\cos^mx\sin nx\,dx$ and hence deduce the value of $\int_0^{\frac\pi2}\cos^5x\sin3x\,dx$.
A function $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and $f$ assumes only rational values on $[0,1]$. Prove that $f$ is a constant function.
If $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ be $n$ positive real numbers such that $a_1\le a_2\le\dots\le a_n$, then show that $a_1\le(a_1a_2\dots a_n)^{1/n}\le a_n$.
State the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. If $a,b,c$ be three positive real numbers, not all equal, prove that $\frac{bc}{b+c}+\frac{ca}{c+a}+\frac{ab}{a+b}<\frac{a+b+c}2$.
If $n$ is a positive integer, prove that $\frac1{2\sqrt{n+1}}<\frac{1.3.5\dots(2n-1)}{2.4.6\dots2n}<\frac1{\sqrt{2n+1}}$.
State the De Moivre's theorem. Find the product of all the values of $(1+i)^{4/5}$.
State and prove the remainder theorem.
Find the remainder when $x^5+x^4-2x^3+3x^2+5x-5$ is divided by $(x-1)(x+2)$.
Solve the equation $x^4-6x^3+18x^2-24x+16=0$ given that the equation has two roots of the form $\alpha+i\alpha$ and $\beta+i\beta$.
State the Descarte's rule of signs. Apply Descarte's rule of signs to find the minimum number of complex roots of the equation $x^7-3x^3+x^2=0$.
Find the values of $k$ for which the equation $x^3-12x^2+45x+k=0$ may have multiple roots and solve the equation in each case.
When is a system of $m$ linear equations in $n$ variables called consistent? Determine whether the following system of linear equations is consistent: $y-4z=8$, $2x-3y+z=1$, $8x-5y+3z=1$.

Discuss the role of free variables in the uniqueness of solution of a consistent system of linear equations. Check whether the solution is unique for the following system: $3x-4y+2z=0$, $-9x+12y-6z=0$, $-6x+8y-4z=0$.

Can every vector $b\in\mathbb R^4$ be written as a linear combination of the columns of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&3&0&3\\-1&-1&-1&1\\0&-4&2&-8\\2&0&3&-1\end{pmatrix}$? Discuss the consistency of the equation $Ax=b$, for each $b\in\mathbb R^4$.
Find the values of $c$ for which the vectors $\begin{pmatrix}1\\5\\-3\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}-2\\-9\\6\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}3\\c\\-9\end{pmatrix}$ are linearly dependent.
What is the null space $N$ of an $n\times n$ matrix $A$? Show that $N$ is a subspace of $\mathbb R^n$.

Define column space of a matrix. Find a basis for the null sapce and a basis for the column space of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&4&8&-3&-7\\-1&2&7&3&4\\-2&2&9&5&5\\3&6&9&-5&-2\end{pmatrix}$. Also find the rank of $A$.

Let $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be given by $T(u)=(x+3y,7x+5y,3x+y)$, for $u=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$. Determine whether $T$ is a linear transformation. Is $T$ one-one? Does $T$ map $\mathbb R^2$ onto $\mathbb R^3$?
What do you mean by the rank and nullity of a linear transformation? State Rank-Nullity theorem for a linear transformation $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$.
When is a set $A=\{u_1,u_2,\dots,u_k\}$ of vectors in $\mathbb R^n$ called an orthogonal set? If $A$ is an orthogonal set, then show that $A$ is a basis for a certain subspace of $\mathbb R^n$.
Obtain an orthonormal basis for the column space of $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-5&1\\1&1&1\\-1&5&-2\\3&-7&8\end{pmatrix}$.

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with distinct eigenvalues $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_k$ $(1\le k\le n)$. If $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_k$ are the corresponding eigenvectors, then show that the set $S=\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_k\}$ is linearly independent. If $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_k$ are not all distinct, then does $S$ still remain linearly independent? Justify.
Check whether the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&2&-1\\1&3&-1\\-1&-2&2\end{pmatrix}$ is diagonalizable and diagonalize $A$, if possible.
If $a,b,c$ are positive real numbers and $a+b+c=1$, show that $8abc\le(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)\le\frac8{27}$.
For any positive integer $n$, prove that $\frac{1.3.5\dots(2n+1)}{2.4.6\dots2n}<2\sqrt{n+1}$.
Find the maximum value of $a^4b^5$, where $a,b$ are positive real numbers satisfying $5a+4b=18$.
Find the modulus and amplitude of $z=1+i\cot\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$ and express $z$ in polar form.
State the De Moivre's theorem. Use it to prove that $2i\sin73\alpha=u^{73}-\frac1{u^{73}}$, provided that $2i\sin\alpha=u-\frac1u$.
Express $x^4-3x^3+10x^2$ as a polynomial in $x-3$. Also find $f(x+3)$.
Construct a biquadratic equation with real coefficients, two of whose roots are $3i\pm\sqrt2$.
Solve the equation $x^4-5x^3-30x^2+40x+64=0$, provided that the roots are in geometric progression.
What do you mean by a reciprocal equation? Solve the equation $6x^4+35x^3+32x^2+35x+6=0$.
Show that the special roots of the equation $x^{14}-1=0$ are the non-real roots of $x^7+1=0$.
Solve the equation $x^3+3x^2-3=0$ by Cardan's method.
Find the solution(s), if there is any, of the system of linear equations $x+3y-5z=4$, $x+4y-8z=7$, $3x+7y-9z=6$ and check if the solution is unique.

When is an indexed set of vectors $\{v_1,v_2,\dots,v_k\}$ of $\mathbb R^n$ $(k<n)$ said to be linearly independent? Examine if the columns of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&4&-3&0\\-2&-7&5&1\\-4&-5&7&5\end{pmatrix}$ form a linearly independent set.
Find a respective basis for the null space and column space of the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1&7&3&9\\-2&2&-2&7&5\\-5&9&3&3&4\\-2&6&6&3&7\end{pmatrix}$. Also find the rank of the matrix $A$.
Construct a $3\times3$ matrix $A$ and two non-zero vectors $b,c\in\mathbb R^3$ such that $b\notin\mathrm{Col}(A)$ but $c\in\mathrm{Nul}(A)$.
Define eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix $A$. What do you mean by eigenspace of $A$ corresponding to an eigenvalue.

Prove that the eigenvectors $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_k$ corresponding to distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\dots,\lambda_k$ of an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ are linearly independent. Does the result hold if $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\dots,\lambda_k$ are not all distinct? Justify.
Suppose that the matrix of a linear transformation $T:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ has orthonormal columns. Show that $T$ preserves the lengths and orthogonality of vectors.
Use Gram-Schmidt process to obtain an orthonormal basis for the column space of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-10&13&7&-11\\2&1&-5&3\\-6&3&13&-3\\16&-16&-2&5\\2&1&-5&-7\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of an $n\times n$ orthogonal matrix $A$. Show that $\frac1\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A^T$.
Evaluate $\lim_{x\to a}\cos x$ by using $(\epsilon-\delta)$ definition of the limit of a function.
If $\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=l$ and $\lim_{x\to a}g(x)=m(\ne0)$ then prove that $\lim_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\frac lm$.
Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous such that for $c\in(a,b)$, $f(c)\ne0$. Show that $f(x)$ has the same sign as that of $f(c)$ in some neighbourhood of $c$.
A function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}\cos\frac1x&\text{for }x\ne0\\0&\text{for }x=0\end{cases}$ Is $f$ continuous at $x=0$? Support your answer.

A function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfies the condition $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$. If $f$ is continuous at one point $c\in\mathbb R$, then prove that $f$ is continuous at every point in $\mathbb R$.
State and prove nested intervals theorem.
Prove that the sequence $\{x_n\}$ defined by $x_1=\sqrt2$ and $x_{n+1}=\sqrt{2x_n}$ for all $n\ge1$ converges to 2.
Prove that a sequence of real numbers is convergent iff it is a Cauchy sequence.
Give an example of a sequence of rational numbers that converges to an irrational number.
Prove that a point $x$ is a limit point of a set $A$ in $\mathbb R$ iff every neighbourhood of $x$ contains infinitely many points of $A$.
Let $S$ be a non-empty subset of $\mathbb R$ and $T=\{-x:x\in S\}$. Prove that $T$ is bounded and $\sup T=-\inf S$ and $\inf T=-\sup S$.
State Archimedean property of $\mathbb R$. Prove that if $x\in\mathbb R$ and $x>0$ then there exists a natural number $n$ such that $0<\frac1n<x$.
If $y=x^{2n}$ where $n$ is a positive integer, then show that $y_n=2^n\{1.3.5.\cdots.(2n-1)\}x^n$.
State and prove Rolle's theorem and give its geometrical interpretation.
In the Mean Value Theorem, $f(x+h)=f(x)+hf'(x+\theta h)$, show that $\theta$ is independent of $x$ where $f(x)$ is given by $f(x)=a+bx+cm^x$.
State L. Hospital's theorem and hence evaluate $\lim_{x\to0}\left(\frac{\tan x}x\right)^{\frac1x}$.
Find the constants $a$ and $b$ so that $\lim_{\theta\to0}\frac{\theta(1+a\cos\theta)-b\sin\theta}{\theta^3}=1$.
If $I_n=\int x^n\sqrt{a-x}\,dx$ then prove that $I_n=\frac{2na}{2n+3}I_{n-1}-\frac{2x^n}{2n+3}(a-x)^{\frac32}$ and hence evaluate $\int_0^ax^3\sqrt{ax-x^2}\,dx$.
State and prove Cauchy's Mean Value theorem and deduce Lagrange's Mean Value theorem from this theorem.

Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Locate and classify the regular and irregular singular points of the ODE
\[x^2(x-2)^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+9(x-2)\frac{dy}{dx}+(x+6)y=0.\]
Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Transform the second order linear ODE $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+P(x)\frac{dy}{dx}+Q(x)y=R(x)$ by changing the independent variable from $x$ to $z$ into $\frac{d^2y}{dz^2}+P_1\frac{dy}{dz}+Q_1y=R_1$ where
\[P_1=\frac{\frac{d^2z}{dx^2}+P\frac{dz}{dx}}{(\frac{dz}{dx})^2},\quad Q_1=\frac{Q}{(\frac{dz}{dx})^2}\quad\text{and}\quad R_1=\frac{R}{(\frac{dz}{dx})^2}.\]
Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Solve the following second order linear ODE with variable coefficients:
\[\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}-\cot x\frac{dy}{dx}-y\sin^2x=\cos x-\cos^3x.\]
Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Comment on the number of independent arbitrary constants within the general solution of the following simultaneous equations:

where $D\equiv\frac d{dt}$.
Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

How to find the general solution of the simultaneous differential equation of type II:
\[\frac{dx}{P(x,y,z)}=\frac{dy}{Q(x,y,z)}=\frac{dz}{R(x,y,z)}?\]
Hence find the general solution of the following simultaneous differential equation:
\[\frac{dx}{x+y-xy^2}=\frac{dy}{x^2y-x-y}=\frac{dz}{z(y^2-x^2)}.\]
Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Solve the following system of two linear homogeneous differential equations with constant coefficients using eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the matrix:

Unit-II (Differential Equations-II) (Full Marks: 30) question number 1 and any two from the rest.
Find the general solution of $[(x+2)D^2-(2x+5)D+2]y=(1+x)e^x$, $D^n\equiv\frac{d^n}{dx^n}$ by the method of operational factors.

Define central force. A particle is let fall from rest from a point outside the earth at a distance $b$ from the centre. Prove that the square of the velocity of the particle on reaching the centre is $ga(3-\frac{2a}b)$, where $a$ is the radius of the earth and $g$ is the value of gravity at its surface.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.
Obtain the expressions for tangential and normal accelerations of a particle moving in a plane curve.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.
A particle describes a catenary under a force which acts parallel to the axis. To find the law of force and the velocity at any point of the path.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.
Obtain the pedal equation of central orbit.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.
A particle describes an equiangular spiral $r=ae^{m\theta}$ with constant velocity. Find the components of velocity and of acceleration along the radius vector and perpendicular to it.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.

If a particle describes a circle of radius $a$ under a force from a point at distance $c\ (<a)$ from the centre, show that the force varies as
\[r\,(r^2+a^2-c^2)^{-3}.\]
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.

A particle subjected to the central acceleration $(\frac{\mu}{r^3}+f)$ is projected from an apse at a distance $a$ with a velocity $\frac{\sqrt{\mu}}a$. Prove that at any subsequent time $t$, $r=a-\frac12ft^2$.
Unit-I [Dynamics of a Particle (Marks: 30)] Answer any three questions.
Find the equation of a trajectory when a particle is projected with a velocity $u$ at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizon in a medium whose resistance is $mk\times(\text{velocity})$.
Define astatic equilibrium. Prove that the astatic centre is a fixed point.
A number of coplanar forces acting on a rigid body reduces to a single force only. Write down the equation of the line of action of their resultant (Define explicitly the parameters involved).
Three forces $P,Q,R$ act along the sides of the triangle formed by the lines $x+y=1$, $y-x=1$, $y=2$. Find the equation of the line of action and the magnitude of their resultant.
State the principle of virtual work for a rigid body and hence deduce the conditions for equilibrium.

Two equal uniform rods AB and AC, each of length $2b$, are freely jointed at A and rest on a smooth vertical circle of radius $a$. Show that, if $2\theta$ be the angle between them, then $b\sin^3\theta=a\cos\theta$.

A solid hemisphere is supported by a string fixed to a point on its rim and to a point on a smooth vertical wall with which the curved surface of the hemisphere is in contact. If $\theta,\phi$ are the inclinations of the string and the plane base of the hemisphere to the vertical, prove that $\tan\phi=\frac38+\tan\theta$.
Obtain the equations of the central axis of a given system of non-coplanar forces acting on a rigid body.

Forces $X,Y,Z$ act along the three straight lines $y=b,z=-c$; $z=c,x=-a$; $x=a,y=-b$ respectively; show that they will have a single resultant if
\[\frac aX+\frac bY+\frac cZ=0.\]
If $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A)=P(B)=1$, then show that $P(A+B)=P(AB)=1$.
What is the probability of an odd sum when two dice are thrown?
If $F(x)$ denotes the distribution function of a random variable $X$, then prove that $F(\infty)=1$.
Define Poisson process and give an example.
If $X$ is a $\beta_2(l,m)$ variate, then show that $Y=1/X$ is a $\beta_2(m,l)$ variate.
Define the moment generating function of a random variable $X$ and find it for the binomial $(n,p)$ distribution.
If $X$ is a non-negative random variable having mean $m$, prove by using Tchebycheff's inequality that, for any $\tau>0$, $P(X\ge\tau m)\le1/\tau$.
Using the axioms of mathematical probability, deduce the classical formula of probability.

If $\{A_n\}$ is a monotonic non-decreasing sequence of events, then prove that
\[P(\lim_{n\to\infty}A_n)=\lim_{n\to\infty}P(A_n).\]
Two urns contain respectively 3 white, 7 red, 15 black balls, and 10 white, 6 red, 9 black balls. One ball is drawn from each urn. Find the probability that both the balls are of the same colour.
Define stochastic independence of two events. Show that if two events $A$ and $B$ are independent, then $A$ and $\bar B$ are independent.

The chance that a doctor will diagnose a certain disease correctly is 60\%. The chance that a patient will die under his/her treatment after correct diagnosis is 40\% and the chance of death by wrong diagnosis is 70\%. A patient of the doctor who had the disease died. What is the chance that his/her disease was diagnosed correctly?
If $F(x)$ denotes the distribution function of a random variable $X$, then show that (i) $P(a<X<b)=F(b-0)-F(a)$ and (ii) $P(a\le X\le b)=F(b)-F(a-0)$.

Find the value of the constant $k$ such that
\[f(x)=\begin{cases}kx(1-x)&0<x<1\\0&\text{elsewhere}\end{cases}\]
is a probability density function corresponding to a random variable $X$. Find the distribution function of $X$ and compute $P(X>1/2)$.
A point $P$ is taken at random on a line segment $AB$ of length $2a$. Find the probability that the area of the rectangle $AP.PB$ will exceed $a^2/2$.

The joint probability density function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by
\[f(x,y)=\begin{cases}k(3x+y)&1<x<3,\ 0<y<2,\\0&\text{elsewhere.}\end{cases}\]
Find the value of the constant $k$ and calculate $P(X+Y<2)$. Examine if $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

If $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n$ are mutually independent random variables each uniformly distributed over $(0,1)$, prove that the probability density function of $X=X_1X_2\cdots X_n$ is
\[\frac1{(n-1)!}\left[\log\left(\frac1x\right)\right]^{n-1},\quad(0<x<1).\]
Hence deduce the probability density function of the geometric mean $(X_1X_2\cdots X_n)^{1/n}$.

If $X$ is a continuous random variable having spectrum $-\infty<x<\infty$ and distribution function $F(x)$, then show that
\[E(X)=\int_0^\infty G(x)\,dx,\]
provided $xG(x)\to0$ as $x\to\infty$, where $G(x)=1-F(x)-F(-x)$.

Show that the characteristic function for the Pascal distribution, given by,
\[f_i=(1-\lambda)\lambda^i,\quad i=0,1,2,\ldots,\]
is $[1-\mu(e^{it}-1)]^{-1}$, where $\mu=\lambda/(1-\lambda)>0$.
Find the mode of a binomial $(4,1/4)$ variate.

Define correlation coefficient $\rho(X,Y)$ between two random variables $X$ and $Y$. If $X$ and $Y$ are uncorrelated, find the correlation coefficient between the linear combinations $a_1X+b_1Y$ and $a_2X+b_2Y$.

The probability density function of a continuous bivariate distribution is given by
\[f(x,y)=\begin{cases}x+y&0<x<1,\ 0<y<1,\\0&\text{elsewhere.}\end{cases}\]
Find the regression curves for the means of $X$ and $Y$.

If, for any pair of linearly dependent random variables $X$ and $Y$, we set $U=X\cos\alpha+Y\sin\alpha$ and $V=-X\sin\alpha+Y\cos\alpha$, then prove that $V$ will be constant (i.e., it has a one-point distribution) if $\tan\alpha=\rho\sigma_y/\sigma_x$. Here, $\alpha$ is a constant and $\sigma_x$ ($\sigma_y$) is the standard deviation of $X$ ($Y$).
When is a sequence of random variables $\{X_n\}$ said to be asymptotically normal? State the Central limit theorem for the case of equal components and show that it implies the law of large numbers.
State the limit theorem for characteristic functions and use it to show that the Poisson distribution is a limit of the Binomial distribution.
Define convergence in probability for a sequence of random variables $\{X_n\}$ and state the law of large numbers for the case of equal components.

If $f$ denotes the frequency ratio of successes in a Bernoullian sequence of $n$ trials with probability of success $p$, then prove that
\[f\xrightarrow{\mathrm{in}\ p}p\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.\]

What do you mean by scalar, vector, and tensor fields? Define covariant, contravariant, and mixed tensors, their order, and rank. Transform the covariant components of a tensor field $(2x+y,xyz,(x+y)^2z)$ in Cartesian coordinates to components in spherical polar coordinates.

Define inner multiplication, contraction, and quotient law of tensor fields. If $A_l^{pq}$ and $B_{rst}^{ij}$ are two tensor fields, examine which one among their sum, difference $A_l^{pq}\pm B_{rst}^{ij}$, and the product $A_l^{pq}B_{rst}^{ij}$ is a tensor field. Justify your answer. Prove that the contraction of $B_iC^j$ is a scalar field.
If $\Phi$ be a scalar field and $A_p$ be a covariant tensor field, examine which of the $\frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial x^l},\frac{\partial A_p}{\partial x^q}$ is a tensor field?

A field variable $A(i,j,k)$ is such that in the coordinate system $x^p$, $A(i,j,k)B_r^{pq}=C_i^q$ where $B_r^{pq}$ is an arbitrary tensor field and $C_i^q$ is a mixed $(1,1)$ tensor field. Examine whether $A(i,j,k)$ is a tensor field.

Define symmetric and skew-symmetric tensors. Prove that every tensor field can be expressed as the sum of symmetric and skew-symmetric tensors in a pair of covariant or contravariant indices. If $\Phi=a_{pq}A^pA^q$, show that $\Phi$ can be expressed as $\Phi=b_{ij}A^iA^j$, where $b_{ij}$ is a symmetric tensor field.

Define line element on a curve in $\mathbb R^n$ in terms of inner product of tensor fields. Examine the nature of the tensor field involved there. Define associated tensors corresponding to those tensor fields. Give the interpretation of these tensors in $\mathbb R^3$. Find the expressions for metric tensors on the spherical and cylindrical surfaces of unit radii.

Define Christoffel's symbols of first and second kind. Evaluate the expressions for Christoffel's first- and second-kind symbols in orthogonal curvilinear coordinates in terms of partial derivatives of metric tensors. Hence obtain their expressions for cartesian coordinate systems.

Define covariant derivatives of tensor fields. Is there any difference between partial and covariant derivatives of a tensor field? When are they same if your answer is affirmative? Prove that the covariant double derivative of a covariant vector field is not commutative, in general.
Answer \emph{any ten} questions. Provide a clear and complete justification for each answer whenever necessary. Each question carries 2 marks. $(10\times2=20)$
Give an example to show that a subfield $K$ in a field $F$ may not be a vector space over $F$.
Determine whether the set $\{x^3-x,\,2x^2+4,\,-2x^3+3x^2+2x+6\}$ is linearly dependent or independent in $\mathcal P_3(\mathbb R)$:
Give an example of a vector space having 121 elements.
Is the vector space of real numbers $\mathbb R$ over the field of rational numbers $\mathbb Q$ finite-dimensional?
Find the row rank of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}10&0&-8\\2&-4&3\\-5&7&6\end{pmatrix}$. \textit{[A faint mark immediately before 7 is indistinct.]}
Prove or disprove: If a linear transformation $T:V\to W$ is one-to-one, then the only vector $x\in V$ such that $T(x)=\theta_W$ is $x=\theta_V$.
Check whether the function $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ defined by $T(a_1,a_2)=(|a_1|,a_2)$ is linear or not.
Find $T(a,b)$, where $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ represents the projection onto the $y$-axis along the $x$-axis.

Let $V$ be a vector space with the ordered basis $\beta=\{v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n\}$. Define $v_0=\theta_V$, and let $T:V\to V$ be a linear transformation such that $T(v_j)=v_j+v_{j-1}$, for $j=1,2,\ldots,n$. Find the matrix representation $[T]_\beta$.
What is the necessary condition on $m$ and $n$ such that the vector spaces $\mathcal P_n(F)$ and $\mathcal P_m(F)$ are isomorphic, where $F$ is a field?
Does there exist a singular change-of-basis matrix from one ordered basis $B_1$ to another ordered basis $B_2$ in a vector space?
Can a finite-dimensional vector space have a dual space of a different dimension?
Let $\beta=\{(2,1),(3,1)\}$ be an ordered basis for $\mathbb R^2$. Find two linear functionals $f_1$ and $f_2$ that form a minimal generating set for the dual space $(\mathbb R^2)^*$.
Can the row vectors of a nonsingular matrix $A$ form a basis for the row space of $A$?

Let $V=\{(a_1,a_2):a_1,a_2\in\mathbb R\}$. For $(a_1,a_2),(b_1,b_2)\in V$ and $c\in\mathbb R$, define
\[(a_1,a_2)+(b_1,b_2)=(a_1+2b_1,a_2+3b_2)\quad\text{and}\quad c(a_1,a_2)=(ca_1,ca_2).\]
Is $V$ a vector space over $\mathbb R$ with these operations? Justify your answer.

Prove that $W_1=\{(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathbb F^n:a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n=0\}$ is a subspace and $W_1=\{(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathbb F^n:a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n=1\}$ is not a subspace. \textit{[The scan repeats \(W_1\), with ink on the second subscript.]}

Let $W$ be a subspace of a vector space $V$ over a field $\mathbb F$. Prove that the set $S=\{v+W:v\in V\}$ with respect to addition and scalar multiplication by scalars of $F$ given by $(v_1+W)+(v_2+W)=(v_1+v_2+W)$ and $a(v_1+W)=av_1+W$ for all $a\in\mathbb F$ is a vector space over $F$.
Give an example of three linearly dependent vectors in $R^3$ such that none of the three is a multiple of another.
Prove that $L(\{x\})=\{ax:a\in\mathbb F\}$ for any vector $x$ in a vector space over a field $F$. Interpret this result geometrically in $R^3$.
Let $V$ be a vector space with dimension $n$. Show that every linearly independent subset of $V$ can be extended to a basis for $V$.
Find a basis for the subspace $W$ of $M_{n\times n}(F)$ of all upper triangular $n\times n$ matrices. What is the dimension of $W$?

Consider the subspaces $W_1=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&a\end{bmatrix}\in V:a,b,c\in\mathbb F\right\}$, and $W_2=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}0&a\\-a&b\end{bmatrix}\in V:a,b\in\mathbb F\right\}$ of $V=M_{2\times2}(\mathbb F)$. Find the dimensions of $W_1$, $W_2$, $W_1+W_2$, and $W_1\cap W_2$ respectively.
Prove that there exists a linear transformation $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ such that $T(1,1)=(1,0,2)$ and $T(2,3)=(1,-1,4)$. What is $T(8,11)$?
Find the rank and nullity of the linear mapping $G:\mathbb R^5\to\mathbb R^3$ defined by $G(x,y,z,s,t)=(x+2y+2z+s+t,x+2y+3z+2s-t,3x+6y+8z+5s-t)$. Is the mapping nonsingular? Justify your answer.

Suppose $V$ is a vector space of dimension $n$ and $T$ be a linear operator on $V$ with $\operatorname{rank}T^2=\operatorname{rank}T$. Then find $\ker T\cap\operatorname{Im}T$. Hence, show that $V$ is a direct sum of $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{Im}T$.

Let $T$ be a linear operator on a finite-dimensional vector space $V$, and let $\beta$ and $\beta'$ be two ordered bases for $V$. Suppose that $Q$ is the change of coordinate matrix that changes $\beta$-coordinates into $\beta'$-coordinates. Then show that $[T]_{\beta'}=Q^{-1}[T]_\beta Q$.

Let $V$ and $W$ be vector spaces, and let $T:V\to W$ be a linear and invertible transformation. Show that $T^{-1}:W\to V$ is linear. For the linear transformation $T:\mathcal P_1(\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R^2$ defined by $T(a+bx)=(a,a+b)$, find the formula for $T^{-1}$.

Let $T:\mathcal P_3(\mathbb R)\to\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$ be the linear transformation defined by $T(f(x))=f'(x)$, and let $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be the standard ordered bases for $\mathcal P_3(\mathbb R)$ and $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$, respectively. For the polynomial $p(x)=2-4x+x^2+3x^3\in\mathcal P_3(\mathbb R)$, verify that $[T(p(x))]_\gamma=[T]_\beta^\gamma[p(x)]_\beta$.
For subspaces $W_1$ and $W_2$ in a vector space $V$ over a field $F$, show that $(W_1+W_2)^0=W_1^0\cap W_2^0$.
Let $V=\mathbb R^3$, and consider the basis $\{f_1(x,y,z)=x-2y,\ f_2(x,y,z)=x+y+z,\ f_3(x,y,z)=y-3z\}$ of $V^*$. Then find a basis for $V$ for which $\{f_1,f_2,f_3\}$ is the dual basis.

Consider the vector spaces $V=\mathcal P_1(\mathbb R)$ and $W=\mathbb R^2$ with respective standard ordered bases \textit{[two basis labels overwritten and partly obscured]}. Define $T:V\to W$ by $T(p(x))=(p(0)-2p(1),p(0)+p'(0))$, where $p'(x)$ is the derivative of $p(x)$. Compute $[T^t]_{\beta^*}^{\gamma^*}$.
Define pointwise and uniform convergence of a sequence of functions $\{f_n\}$.
If $f_n(x)=n^2x^2e^{-nx}$, determine whether the sequence $\{f_n\}$ is uniformly convergent on $[0,\infty)$.
Show that the sequence $\{\tan^{-1}nx\}$ is pointwise convergent on $\mathbb R$.
Let $\{f_n\}$ be a pointwise convergent sequence of bounded functions on $D\subseteq\mathbb R$. Show that its limit function may not be bounded on $D$.

If a sequence $\{f_n\}$ of Riemann integrable functions converges uniformly to a function $f$ on a closed and bounded interval $[a,b]$, show that $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$ and the sequence $\{\int_a^b f_n\}$ converges to $\int_a^b f$.
State and prove Cauchy's principle for uniform convergence of series of functions.
Show that the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^{n-1}\cos nx}{k^2-n^2}$ (where $k\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Z$) is uniformly convergent on any closed and bounded interval.
Check if the series $1+x+x^2+x^3+\cdots$ is uniformly convergent on $[0,1)$.
Let a series $\sum f_n$ of continuous functions be uniformly convergent on $D\subseteq\mathbb R$. Prove that its sum function is continuous on $D$.
Show that the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty(-1)^n(x^n-x^{n+1})$ converges uniformly on $[0,1]$ but $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty(x^n-x^{n+1})$ does not converge uniformly on $[0,1]$.
If a power series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ diverges for $x=c$, show that it diverges for all $x\in\mathbb R$ with $|x|>|c|$.

State Cauchy-Hadamard Theorem for power series. If $\sum a_n$ is an absolutely convergent series of real numbers, then show that $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^n$ converges absolutely on $[-1,1]$.
Find the radius and interval of convergence of the power series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{n^5+1}{(n^7+1)3^n}x^n$.
What do you mean by a real analytic function? Explain with example.
Prove or disprove: All functions which are infinitely many times differentiable on an interval are real analytic functions.
Prove that if $\lim_{(x,y)\to(a,b)}f(x,y)$ exists finitely then $f(x,y)$ is necessarily bounded in some deleted neighbourhood of the point $(a,b)$.
Prove that if the double limit $\lim_{(x,y)\to(a,b)}f(x,y)=l$ and one repeated limit $\lim_{x\to a}\lim_{y\to b}f(x,y)=l'$ exists then $l=l'$.
Show that the function $f(x,y)=\begin{cases}\frac{xy}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}&\text{for }(x,y)\ne(0,0)\\0&\text{for }(x,y)=(0,0)\end{cases}$ is continuous at $(0,0)$.
Prove that if $f(x,y)$ is continuous at a point $(a,b)$ and $f(a,b)>0$, then $f(x,y)>0$ in some neighbourhood of $(a,b)$.

When a function $f(x,y)$ is said to be differentiable at a point $(a,b)$? If $f(x,y)$ is differentiable at a point $(a,b)$, then show that the partial derivatives $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ and $\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ both exist finitely at $(a,b)$.
State and prove a sufficient condition for differentiability of a function of two variables at a point $(a,b)$.
State and prove Young's theorem for equality of two mixed second order partial derivatives of a function $f(x,y)$ at a point $(a,b)$.

Let $f(x_1,x_2)$ be differentiable in a region $R$ and $x_1\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1}+x_2\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2}=nf(x_1,x_2)$ for $(x_1,x_2)$ in $R$. Then show that $f(x_1,x_2)$ is a homogeneous function of degree $n$ in $R$.
State and prove Mean Value Theorem for a function of two variables.
State and prove Implicit function theorem for a function of two variables.

Prove that a necessary condition for a function $f(x,y)$ to have an extreme value at $(a,b)$ is that $\frac{\partial f(a,b)}{\partial x}=0$, $\frac{\partial f(a,b)}{\partial y}=0$, provided these partial derivatives exist.
Show that $f(x,y)=x^4+x^2y+y^2$ has a minimum at $(0,0)$.
Use Lagrange method to find the shortest distance from the point $(2,0)$ to the parabola $y^2=8x$.
Evaluate $\iint_R xy^2(x^2+y^2)\,dx\,dy$ over $R:\{(x,y):0\le x\le a;0\le y\le b\}$.
Evaluate $\iint_E x^2y^2\,dx\,dy$ over the region $E$ bounded by $x\ge0,y\ge0$ and $x^2+y^2\le1$.

\]

\[
x'=ax+by,\qquad y'=cx+dy,
\]
where $a,b,c$ and $d$ are real constants. Discuss the nature of the equilibrium point in the following cases. 
\begin{romanparts}
\item If $a=d$, and $b$ and $c$ are of opposite sign.
\item If $a=d$, and either $b$ or $c=0$.
\item If $a=d$, and $b$ and $c$ are of same sign and such that $\sqrt{bc}<|a|$.
\item If $a=d$, and $b$ and $c$ are of same sign and such that $\sqrt{bc}>|a|$.
\item If $a=-d$, and $ad>bc$.
\item If $a=-d$, and $b$ and $c$ are of same sign
\end{romanparts}

\begin{romanparts}
\item Find the Laplace transform of $f(t)$, where $f(t)=e^{-5t}\sinh 2t+e^{9t}\cos t+t^3e^{-7t}$.
\item Solve the Fredholm integro-differential equation $u'(x)=x^5+\displaystyle\int_0^1tu(t)dt$, $u(0)=1$.
\item What is the value of $g(5)$, where $g(x)=\sin x+\displaystyle\int_0^x\cos(x-t)g(t)dt$.
\item Find the finite Fourier sine transform of $\sin ax$ in $0<x<\pi$.
\item Convert the boundary value problem $y''+\lambda y=0$, $y(0)=1$, $y(1)=0$ into an integral equation.
\item Find the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)$, where $F(s)=\dfrac{se^{-2\pi s/3}}{s^2+1}$.
\item Find the condition for which the integral equation $y(t)=f(t)+5\displaystyle\int_0^1tsy(s)ds$ has infinitely many solutions.

\]

Solve the integral equation $u(x)=x\sin x-\frac12+\frac12\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}u(t)dt$ by using modified Adomian decomposition method.

Let $T:V\to V$ be a linear operator and $m(t)$ is the minimal polynomial of $T$. Prove that $\lambda\in F$ is an eigen value of $T$ if and only if $m(\lambda)=0$.

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ complex matrix such that every nonzero vector in $\mathbb C^n$ is an eigen vector of $A$. Is $A$ a scalar matrix?

Let $\lambda$ be an eigen value of a linear operator $T$ and $G_\lambda$ be the corresponding generalized eigen space. Show that the subspace $G_\lambda$ is $T$-invariant and $\lambda$ is the only eigen value of $T|_{G_\lambda}$.
Let $T:V\to V$ be a linear operator. Prove that nonzero generalized eigen vectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues of $T$ are linearly independent.

Let $T$ be a linear operator on $V$ whose characteristic polynomial splits over $F$, and $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $T$. If a basis for $G_\lambda$ is the union of $q$ disjoint cycles of generalized eigenvectors, prove that $q\geq\dim E_\lambda$. When does the equality hold? Justify.
Let $T:V\to V$ be a nilpotent linear operator. Prove that $k$ is the index of nilpotence of $T$ if and only if $t^k$ is the minimal polynomial of $T$.
Let $T:V\to V$ be a nilpotent operator. Prove that the number of Jordan blocks in a Jordan canonical form is equal to the geometric multiplicity of the eigen value 0.

Let $T$ be a linear operator which has the characteristic polynomial $t^2(t-1)^4$ and the minimal polynomial $t(t-1)^2$. Find all possible Jordan canonical forms of $T$. In each case find the rank and nullity of the matrix; and the dimension of the eigen spaces.

Consider the inner product space $P_2(\mathbb R)$ where the inner product is defined by $\langle p(x),q(x)\rangle=\int_0^1p(x)q(x)dx$ and a linear functional $\phi$ on $P_2(\mathbb R)$ is defined by $\phi(a+bx+cx^2)=a+2b+3c$. Find an orthonormal basis of this inner product space and find $q(x)\in P_2(\mathbb R)$ such that $\phi(p(x))=\langle p(x),q(x)\rangle$. Also find the adjoint of the linear operator $T:P_2(\mathbb R)\to P_2(\mathbb R)$ defined by $\phi(p(x))=p(0)+xp'(x)$.
Let $T:U\to V$ be a linear transformation. Show that $\ker T^*=(\mathit{Im}\,T)^\perp$ and $\ker TT^*=\ker T^*$.

Let $T$ be a normal operator on an Euclidean space $V$. Show that the eigen vectors belonging to two distinct eigen values are orthogonal and the minimal polynomial of $T$ is a product of distinct irreducible factors over $\mathbb R$.
Let $T$ be an unitary operator over a complex inner product space $V$. Prove that $T$ maps every orthonormal basis of $V$ into an orthonormal basis of $V$.

Let $T$ be a linear operator over an Euclidean space $V$. Show that $T$ is symmetric if and only if it is orthogonally diagonalizable.

Find the characteristic values and corresponding orthonormal characteristic functions of following ordinary differential equation
\[
\frac{d^2x}{dy^2}+\lambda x=0.
\]
with boundary conditions
\[
\text{(i) }x(0)=0,\quad x(\pi)=0 \qquad\textit{and}\qquad
\text{(ii) }x'(0)=0,\quad x(\pi/2)=0
\]

Using Green's function, solve the following differential equation
\[
\frac{d^2x}{dy^2}+\omega^2x=f(y).
\]
with boundary conditions $x(0)=0,\ x(\pi/2)=0$
State an existence and uniqueness theorem for solution of a 1st order IVP. With a suitable example show the theorem is sufficient but not necessary.

Show that the interval where the unique solution of the following IVP
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{e^{y^2}-1}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]
subject to the condition $y(-2)=1$, surely exist is $[-2.02,\quad -2.18]$
Use Picard's iteration method to find the first two approximate solution of the following IVP $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\cos x$, subject to $x(0)=0$. Also find how good the approximation is.

State Abel's formula. Hence show that if $f$ and $g$ are two solutions of
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left(P(t)\frac{dx}{dt}\right)+Q(t)x=0,
\]
such that $f$ and $g$ have a common zero then $f$ and $g$ are linearly dependent.

Find the interval of definition of the following IVP
\[
\frac{d^3x}{dt^3}+\frac{x}{t^2-4}=\cos t,\quad
\text{subject to }\quad x'(1)=3\quad x'(1)=0\quad x''(1)=0.
\]

Show that $\{1,t,t^2\}$ are linearly independent over $(-\infty,+\infty)$. Construct two functions $f_1$ and $f_2$ such that they are linearly independent but their Wronskian is zero over $(-\infty,+\infty)$.

What is meant by a fundamental matrix of a linear homogeneous system $\dfrac{dX}{dt}=AX$. Express the coefficient matrix $A$ in terms of fundamental matrix. If
\[
\Phi(t)=\begin{bmatrix}e^{2t}&e^{4t}\\-e^{2t}&e^{4t}\end{bmatrix}
\]
is a fundamental matrix of $\frac{dX}{dt}=AX$., then find $A$.

Solve the following system
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=x+y-1,\qquad \frac{dy}{dt}=y+1
\]
subject to the initial condition $x(0)=1$ and $y(0)=0$.
Find the nature and stability of the critical point of the following system $x'=3x-4y,\ y'=x-y$. Also find and sketch the phase path.
Define matrix exponential function $e^{At}$. If $P^{-1}AP=D$ then show that $e^{At}=Pe^{Dt}P^{-1}$.
State and prove Sturm separation theorem.

Convert the Bessel's equation of order $n$ into the form $x'+p(t)x=0$. Show that if $0\leq n<\frac12$ the distance between two successive zeros of $x(t)$ is less than $\pi$ and tends to $\pi$ as the number of oscillating solution increases.

Show that the Cauchy problem $yu_x-xu_y=0$, $u=f$ on $\Gamma$ has a unique solution in a neighbourhood of $\Gamma$ for every differentiable function $f:\Gamma\to\mathbb R$, where $\Gamma=\{(x,y):x+y=1,x>1\}$.

Find, by the method of characteristics, the integral surface of the following PDE:
\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}+\left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\right)^2=1,\quad
x\in\mathbb R,\ y>0,\ u(x,0)=-x^2.
\]

Find the complete integral of the PDE
\[
u_{xx}-u_{xy}-2u_{yy}+2u_x+2u_y=xy+\sin(x+2y).
\]

Solve the following PDE by Monge's method:
\[
y^2\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}-2y\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x\partial y}
+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial y^2}=u_x+6y.
\]
Find the expression of the Monge cone of the PDE $u_x^2+u_y^2=2021$ at $(1,1,1)$.

Find the number of real characteristic curves of the PDE
\[
\left[a(x,y)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+b(x,y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\right]
\left[c(x,y)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+d(x,y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\right]u=0,\quad ad-bc=0,
\]
where $a,b,c,d$ be four differentiable functions defined on $\mathbb R^2$.

Find the two families of characteristics of
\[
2x^2u_{xx}-5xyu_{xy}+2y^2u_{yy}+2xu_x+2yu_y=0.
\]
Convert the equation to canonical form and hence find $u(x,y)$, given that $u=2x^2-6$ and $u_y=3-x^2$ on $y=1$.

Using appropriate integral transform method, solve the initial boundary value problem (IBVP) described as
\[
\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}=\frac1{c^2}\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial t^2}-\cos(2t),
\quad 0\leq x<\infty,\ 0\leq t<\infty,
\]
BC's: $u(0,t)=0$, $u(x,t)$ is bounded as $x\to\infty$,

IC's: $u(x,0)=0,\ u_t(x,0)=0$.

Using appropriate integral transform method, find the temperature $u(x,t)$ in a semi-infinite rod $0\leq x<\infty$, determined by the PDE
\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=k\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2},\quad x\in(0,\infty),\ t>0,
\]
subject to

IC: $u(x,0)=0,\ 0\leq x<\infty$,

BC's: $u_x(0,t)=-u_0$ (a constant) when $x=0$ and $t>0$;

$u,\ \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}$ both tend to zero as $x\to\infty$.
State maximum-minimum principle for a function $u(x,y)$ which is continuous in a closed region $\overline{\mathbb R}$ and satisfies the Laplace equation $\nabla^2u=0$ in the interior of $\mathbb R$.

Let $u(x,t)$ satisfies the initial boundary value problem (IBVP)
\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=9\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2},\quad x\in(0,1),\ t>0,
\]
BC's: $u(0,t)=u(1,t)=0$,

IC: $u(x,0)=\sin^2(\pi x),\ x\in[0,1]$.

Then, for $x\in(0,1)$ find the value of $u(x,\frac1{2\pi^2})$.

With the help of separation of variables method, obtain the solution of the following initial boundary value problem (IBVP) for the wave equation:

\]
BC's: $u(0,t)=u(\pi,t)=0$,

IC's: $u(x,0)=0,\ u_t(x,0)=2\cos(x)-3\cos(2x)$.
State Cauchy-Kowalevski theorem for a second order linear PDE.

Solve the following interior Dirichlet problem for a circle:

PDE: $\nabla^2u=0,\ 0\leq r<a,\ 0\leq\theta<2\pi$

BC: $u(a,\theta)=f(\theta),\ 0\leq\theta<2\pi$

where $f(\theta)$ is a continuous function on $\partial\mathbb R$.

Hence deduce Poisson's integral formula of the form

u(r,\theta)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\phi=0}^{2\pi}

\]

Find the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)$, where $F(s)=\dfrac{s}{s^2+4s+7}+\dfrac1{(s+3)^4}$.

Find the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the integral equation

Find the resolvent kernel of the Fredholm integral equation

\]
Convert the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+4xy=2$, $y(0)=0$, $y'(1)=1$ to an equivalent integral equation.
Find the inverse Fourier sine transform of $\dfrac{e^{-as}}s$. Hence find the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \dfrac{\sin2x}{x}dx$.
Using Hilbert-Schmidt theorem, solve the integral equation $y(x)=x+\int_0^1(1-3xt)y(t)dt$.

If $f$ and $g$ are piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and of exponential order, then prove that $L\{f*g\}=L\{f\}.L\{g\}$.
Using the above result prove that $\beta(m,n)=\dfrac{\Gamma(m).\Gamma(n)}{\Gamma(m+n)}$.

If $L\{f(t)\}=F(s)$, then prove that $L\{\frac{f(t)}t\}=\displaystyle\int_s^\infty F(x)dx$. Hence evaluate the integral $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-4t}\sin t}{t}dt$. Does the Laplace transform of $\dfrac{\cos at}{t}$ exist?

State Fredholm alternative theorem. Find the conditions for which the integral equation $y(x)=f(x)+\int_0^1k(x,t)y(t)dt$ has infinitely many solutions, where $k(x,t)=(t+1)x$ when $0\leq t\leq x$ and $k(x,t)=(x+1)t$ when $x\leq t\leq1$.

Solve the differential equation $t\dfrac{dx}{dt}-x=1$ by Laplace transform method.
Give an example of a function which is neither piecewise continuous nor of exponential order but whose Laplace transform exists.
Solve the Volterra integral equation $y(x)=x-\int_0^x (x-t)y(t)dt$ by
Solve the Volterra integral equation of first kind $e^{x^2/2}-1=\int_0^x\sin(x-t)u(t)dt$.

Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)$, where $f(x)=1-x^2$ if $|x|<1$ and $f(x)=0$ if $|x|>1$.
Hence using Persaval's identity, evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\left(\dfrac{\sin x-x\cos x}{x^3}\right)^2dx$.
Show that the sets $\emptyset$ and $\mathbb R$ are measurable. Also find their measures.
Find the measures of the following sets: (i) the set of irrationals in $[0,2022]$ (ii) $\{\sin x:0<x<40\pi\}$ (iii) $\{\frac1{n^2}:n\in\mathbb Z\}$ (iv) $\{\frac1{x^2}:0\leq x<\infty\}$
Show that Lebesgue measure is invariant under translations.
Show that if $\mu^*(E)=0$ then $E$ is measurable.
If $B\subset A$ are measurable sets then show that $\mu(A\sim B)=\mu(A)-\mu(B)$
Prove that for any two measurable sets $A$ and $B$ $\mu(A\cup B)+\mu(A\cap B)=\mu(A)+\mu(B)$
Suppose $\{E_n\}$ be a sequence of sets, construct a disjoint sequence of sets $\{F_n\}$ such that $\bigcup E_n=\bigcup F_n$
Prove that there exist sets that are not measurable
Show that $E$ is measurable if and only if $\chi_E$ is measurable.
Show that a Riemann integrable function is Lebesgue integral but converse is not true.

Suppose $\{E_n\}$ be a sequence of disjoint measurable sets such that $\mu(\bigcup E_n)$ is finite and $f$ is bounded and measurable function on it, then show that

\]
Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}f(x)dx$ where $f(x)=\begin{cases}\sin x&\text{if }x\text{ is irrational,}\\\cos x&\text{if }x\text{ is rational}\end{cases}$
State and prove Fatou's Lemma. Show that strict inequality may occur in it.
Show that $f(x)=\dfrac1{x^{1/3}}$ is summable (unbounded Lebesgue integrable) in $[0,1]$ and find $\displaystyle\int_0^1f(x)dx$.
If $f$ is integrable on $[0,1]$ then show that $f$ is finite a.e.
If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are measurable sets then show that $E_1\cup E_2$ is measurable.
If $f$ is summable on $E$ then show that $-f$ is so and $\int_E f\,dx=\int_E(-f)dx$
State Dominated convergence theorem and show that Bounded convergence theorem is a special case of it

Expand $f(z)=\frac1{(z+1)(z+3)}$ in Laurent series in the region $|z|>3$.
Show that if $f(z)=\frac{\phi(z)}{(z-\alpha)^n}$, where $\phi(z)$ is analytic at $\alpha$ and $\phi(\alpha)\ne0$ then $\alpha$ is a pole of $f(z)$ of order $n$.
If $\beta$ be a pole of $f(z)$ of order $m$ and a pole of $g(z)$ of order $n(>m)$ then what kind of a point $\beta$ relative to the function $f(z)+g(z)$.

If a function $f(z)$ is regular in a domain $D$ and if $z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_n,\ldots$ is a sequence of zeros of $f(z)$ having as limit point an interior point $\alpha$ of $D$, then show that $f(z)\equiv0$.

If $\alpha$ be a limit point of the zeros of $f(z)$ and if $f(z)$ is analytic in some deleted neighbourhood $0<|z-\alpha|<\rho$ of $\alpha$, then show that $\alpha$ is an isolated essential singularity of $f(z)$.
Find out the zeros and determine the nature of the singularities of the function $f(z)=\frac{z+2}{z^2}\sin\left(\frac1{z+1}\right)$ and also find the residue at $z=0$.

Assume that $f(z)$ is analytic in $|z|<1$, $f(0)=0$ and $|f(z)|\leq1$. If for a point $\alpha$, $0<|\alpha|<1$ satisfying $|f(\alpha)|=|\alpha|$ then show that $f(z)=e^{i\theta}z$ ($\theta=constant$).
State Cauchy's residue theorem. Using this theorem evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_{|z|=\frac32}\frac{z-1}{z^2+2z}dz$.

Let $f(z)$ be analytic within and on a positively oriented simple closed curve $C$ except for a finite number of poles within $C$ and let $f(z)\ne0$ any where on $C$, then show that

\]

Let $f(z)$ be analytic in $|z|\leq1$ and $|f(z)|<1$ on $|z|=1$. Show that there exists just one point $\beta$ within the circle $|z|=1$ such that $f(\beta)=\beta$.
If a function $f(z)$ has no singularity in the finite z-plane and has a pole of order $m$ at infinity then $f(z)$ must be a rational integral function of degree $m$.
Let $X,Y\in\mathbb R^n$ and let $A=XY^t$. Show that the characteristic polynomial of $A$ is $t^{n-1}(t-\lambda)$ where $\lambda=X^tY$. If $\lambda\ne0$, then prove that $E_0\perp Y$.

Let $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ be the projection of $\mathbb R^2$ on the $x$-axis along the line $y=2x$. Find two nonzero proper $T$-invariant subspaces of $\mathbb R^2$. Is there any other nonzero proper $T$-invariant subspaces?
State and prove the Cayley-Hamilton theorem for linear operators.
Let $m(t)$ be the minimal polynomial of a linear operator $T:V\to V$. Show that $m(t)\mid f(t)$ for every annihilating polynomial $f(t)$ of $T$.
Give an example to show that two matrices may not be similar still they can have the same minimal polynomial. Justify.

Let $M\in M_n(F)$ and let $T:M_n(F)\to M_n(F)$ be defined by $T(A)=MA$. Show that $T$ and $M$ have the same minimal polynomial.
Let $A\in M_n(F)$. Prove that eigen vectors belonging to distinct eigen values of $A$ are linearly independent.
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix with each entry equal to 1. Find the eigen values of $A$ with multiplicities. Hence find a diagonal form of $A$.
Let $T:M_n(\mathbb R)\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be defined by $T(A)=A^t$. Show that 1 and $-1$ are the only eigen values of $T$. Hence or otherwise show that $T$ is diagonalizable.
Show that a linear operator $T:V\to V$ is triangulizable if and only if the characteristic polynomial of $T$ splits into linear factors.
If $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are two distinct eigen values of a linear operator $T$, then show that $G_\lambda\cap G_\mu=\{\theta\}$.
Find the Jordan canonical form of the linear operator $T(p(x))=p'(x)$ on $P_2(\mathbb R)$.

Let $T$ be a linear operator on an inner product space $V$. If $T$ has an eigen value $\lambda$ then show that $\overline\lambda$ is an eigen value of $T^*$.
If $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x,y,z)=2x-3y+4z$, find a vector $Y\in\mathbb R^3$ such that $f(X)=\langle X,Y\rangle$ for all $X\in\mathbb R^3$.
Find the adjoint of the linear operator $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ defined by $T(x,y)=(x-y,2x+y)$.
Prove that eigen vectors belonging to two distinct eigen values of a normal operator are orthogonal.
Show that every eigen value of a self-adjoint linear operator is real.
Prove that a linear operator $T$ on $V$ is unitary if and only if $\|T(v)\|=\|v\|$ for all $v\in V$.

Let $Q$ be a real skew-symmetric matrix. Then show that $I+Q$ is nonsingular.

BC's: $u(0,t)=u(1,t)=0$, $t>0$,

Consider the homogeneous Dirichlet diffusion problem
