Find the optimal simplex table of the following LPP:\par
Maximize $f(x_1,x_2,x_3)=3x_1-2x_2+4x_3$\par
subject to \quad $x_1+2x_2+x_3\le430$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$3x_1\quad\ \ +2x_3\le460$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1+4x_2\qquad\ \ \le420$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$. \par
What will be the effect when\par
\hspace*{1em}(i) a new constraint $3x_1+2x_3\le500$ and\par
\hspace*{1em}(ii) a new constraint $3x_1+2x_3\le400$ is added to the problem?
Distinguish between ordinary linear programming problem and integer linear programming problem.

Find the optimal solution to the LPP:\par
Maximize $f(x_1,x_2)=2x_1+2x_2$\par
subject to \quad $5x_1+3x_2\le8$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1+2x_2\le4$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2\ge0$ and are integers. 
\par\hfill P.T.O.

\begin{center}[ 2 ]\end{center}
State Kuhn-Tucker necessary and sufficient conditions to find a solution of the non-linear programming problem (NLPP).

Use the Kuhn-Tucker necessary and sufficient conditions to solve the following NLPP:\par
Minimize $f(x_1,x_2)=-\log_e x_1-\log_e x_2$\par
subject to \quad $x_1+x_2\le2$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2\ge0$.

Show the following NLPP graphically:\par
Minimize $f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2-2x_1+x_2^2+1$\par
subject to \quad $x_1+x_2\le0$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1^2-4\le0$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2\ge0$.

In a deterministic inventory model where supply is instantaneous and shortages are permitted in the sense of back orders, find mathematical expressions for the optimal lot size and corresponding annual cost.

The purchase manager currently follows EOQ policy of ordering for an item in the stores of his company. The annual demand of the item is 1600 units. Its carrying cost is 40\% of the unit cost where the unit cost is Rs. 400. The ordering cost is Rs. 500 per order. Recently, the vendor supplying that item gives a discount of 10\% in its unit cost if the order size is minimum of 500 units. \par
\hspace*{1em}(i) Find EOQ and the corresponding total cost per year.\par
\hspace*{1em}(ii) Check whether the discount offer given by the vendor can be considered by the purchase manager.
For the queueing model system (M/M/1 : N/FCFS), find the probability of n customers in the system in the form $p_n=\dfrac{(1-\rho)\rho^n}{1-\rho^{N+1}},\ \rho\neq1,\ n=0,1,2,\ldots,N.$

In a railway marshaling yard, goods trains arrive at a rate of 30 trains per day. Assume that the inter arrival time follows an exponential distribution and the service time distribution is also exponential with an average of 36 minutes. Calculate: \par
\hspace*{1em}(i) The probability that the yard is empty.\par
\hspace*{1em}(ii) Average queue length assuming that the line capacity of the yard is 9 trains.

Formulate a compartmental model for diabetes mellitus, stating explicitly the assumptions you make therein. Solve the model equations and state the salient features that one can make out of the analysis.
What is meant by creep and stress relaxation of viscoelastic material?
Obtain the constitutive equation when a spring and a Kelvin element are in series. Show that it qualifies as a solid.
Obtain the differential equation when an arbitrary number of Maxwell units are connected in series, possible including the degenerated units.
Obtain the expressions for velocity and flux for one-dimensional steady flow of Power law fluid past a rigid circular tube. Hence obtain the corresponding expressions for Newtonian fluid.
Define yield stress. Obtain the expression of plug velocity for Casson fluid under constant pressure gradient in unidirectional flow.
Discuss the pulsatile flow of Newtonian fluid in a rigid tube.
Discuss two major hypotheses on brain damage.
Formulate a mathematical model for study of the physiological problem of brain injury, when the head is subjected to impulsive load.
Obtain Gibb's-Duhem relation for a multicomponent thermodynamic system. Deduce the corresponding relation for sea-water, supposing it to be a mixture of salt and pure water.

Derive the following relations in $(T,\ p,\ s)$ variables:\par
\hspace*{1em}i) $\Gamma=\dfrac{T}{C_p}\dfrac{\partial\tau}{\partial T}$\par
\hspace*{1em}ii) $d\eta=\dfrac{C_p}{T}dT-\dfrac{d\tau}{dT}dp-\dfrac{d\mu}{dT}ds.$

Assuming the sea-water to be a two-component mixture of salt and pure water, show that the principle of conservation of mass yields the following equations:
\[\frac{D\rho}{Dt}+\rho\nabla\cdot\vec q=0\quad\text{and}\quad\rho\frac{Ds}{Dt}=-\nabla\cdot\vec I_s.\]
Explain the significance of the quantities $\vec I_s$ and $\vec I_w$ in this connection.
Obtain the boundary conditions at the free ocean surface by taking into account that the mass exchange process across the surface amounts to a flux `b' of pure water in unit time per unit area.

State the assumptions on which the Boussinesq approximation of the governing equations of sea water is derived. Derive the approximate forms of the equation of continuity, equation of motion and equation of energy.

Assuming sea-water to be a viscous compressible heat-conducting fluid, derive the equation of conservation of energy in the form
\[\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\left(\rho E_m\right)=-\nabla\cdot\vec I_E.\]
Explain the significance of different components of $E_m$ and $\vec I_E$.

When is sea-water said to be vertically stratified? Show that a vertically stratified fluid is in stable mechanical equilibrium if
\[\frac{g}{\rho}\frac{dp}{dz}+\frac{g^2}{c^2}<0.\]
Obtain the equation of conservation of energy for linearized small amplitude wave motion of ocean water.

Show that the problem of determination of frequencies of free oscillations in a horizontally unbounded ocean of constant depth may be reduced to the problem of solution of independent eigen value problems.\par
Assuming sea-water to be incompressible and having a uniform V\"ais\"al\"a frequency, find approximately the eigen values of problem $V$.
Discuss the spread of a plane free jet. Show that the mass flux increases in the downstream as $x^{\frac13}$ where $x$ is the distance measured downstream from the slit of the jet.
Discuss the Blasius solution of the boundary layer flow on a flat plate and calculate the coefficient of skin friction.
Describe Maccormack's technique for the solution of unsteady two dimensional Euler equations.
Discuss MAC method for primitive variables approach using staggered grid. Also derive the discretized Poison equation in this formulation.

Transform the following differential equation:
\[\frac{\partial U}{\partial t}+\frac{\partial F}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial G}{\partial y}=0,\]
from $(x,y)$ plane to $(\xi,\eta)$ plane and write it in strong conservative form where $\xi=\xi(x,y),\eta=\eta(x,y),t=t.$

Find the compact high-order formulas for the wall boundary conditions at all the four walls in the case of flow in a rectangular cavity while solving using stream-function vorticity equations for viscous, incompressible flow.

Distinguish Lie group of point transformations (LGPT) admitted by a differential equation and continuous group of equivalence transformations admitted by a family of differential equations.\par
Derive expression for $\phi^{(i)},\ \mu f^{(k)},\ \mu g^{(k)}$ in the prolongation of infinitesimal generator (IG) $\hat X=\xi\partial_x+\tau\partial_t+\phi\partial_u+\mu f\partial_f+\mu g\partial_g$ for the continuous group of equivalence transformations admitted by the family of equation $f(u)u_t=g(u_x)u_{xx}$. 
\begin{center}\textbf{OR}\end{center}
Derive determining equations and find explicit forms of $\xi,\ \tau,\ f,\ g$ containing atleast two arbitrary constants involved in the IG $\hat X=\xi\partial_x+\tau\partial_t+(fu+g)\partial_u$ by Lie group of symmetry transformations (LGST) admitted by the wave equation $u_{tt}=u_{xx}$. It may be assumed that $\xi,\ \tau,\ f,\ g$ are multinomial in $x$ and $t$ of order atmost 2.

Verify whether the generalized KdV equation $u_t+u^{\nu}u_x+u_{xxx}=0$ admits one parameter LGST generated by the IG $\hat X=x\partial_x+3t\partial_t-\dfrac{2}{\nu}u\partial_u$. Reduce the partial differential equation mentioned above to an ordinary differential equation with the help of similarity transformations corresponding to the given IG $\hat X$, if yes.

Establish the recursion relation
\[\phi^{(k)}_{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_{k-1}i_k}=D_{i_k}\left[\phi^{(k-1)}_{i_1\ldots i_{k-1}}\right]-D_{i_k}\left[\xi_j\right]u_{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_{k-1}j}\]
involved in the prolongation of IG for LGPT defined on geometric space whose points are described by $(x_1,\ldots,x_n,u)$ where the variable $u$ may be a function of other variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. Here $i_1,\ldots,i_k=1,2,\ldots,n,\ k\ge1.$\par
Provide the statement in MATHEMATICA for getting prolongation of a given IG $\hat X=\xi\partial_x+\tau\partial_t+\phi\partial_u$.

What do you mean by similarity variables associated with a LGST generated by the IG $\hat X=\xi\partial_x+\eta\partial_y+\phi\partial_u$ admitted by a differential equation
\[F\left(x,\ y,\ u,\ u_x,\ u_y,\ u_{xx},\ u_{xy},\ u_{yy}\right)=0\,?\]
Find similarity variables for $\hat X=y\partial_x+\left(x+y^2\right)\partial_u.$ 
\par\hfill P.T.O.

\begin{center}( 2 )\end{center}

Find the group invariant solution of heat equation $u_t=u_{xx}$ corresponding to the IG
\[\hat X=xt\partial_x+t^2\partial_t-\left(\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac t2\right)u\partial_u.\]
Provide statement for obtaining similarity variables for $\hat X$ mentioned above with the help of MATHEMATICA.

Show that the heat conduction equation $u_t=u_{xx},\ (x,\ t)\in\mathbb R^2$ admits six parameter Lie group of point transformations generated by $\hat X=\xi\partial_x+\tau\partial_t+\phi\partial_u$, where $\xi=\kappa+\beta x+\delta t+\gamma xt,\ \tau=\alpha+2\beta t+\gamma t^2,\ \phi=\left\{\lambda-\dfrac12\delta x-\gamma\left(\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac t2\right)\right\}u.$ Find the values of six parameters $\alpha,\ \beta,\ \gamma,\ \delta,\ \lambda$ whenever the domain is restricted to $x\ge0,\ t\ge0.$

Discuss the propagation of EM waves in a cold electron (ions form the background) plasma in presence of a uniform magnetostatic field. Show that the dispersion relation can be obtained in the form
\[\left(S\sin^2\theta+P\cos^2\theta\right)\eta^4-\left[RL\sin^2\theta+SP\left(1+\cos^2\theta\right)\right]\eta^2+PRL=0,\]
where $\theta$ is the angle of the wave vector with the magnetic field $\vec B\equiv B_0\hat z$, $\eta$ is the index of refraction and other symbols have their usual meanings with $R=S+D,\ L=S-D,\ S=\dfrac12(R+L),\ D=\dfrac12(R-L).$\par
Hence obtain the Appleton -- Hartree equation.

The electric field perturbation of an EM wave propagating along the constant magnetic field $B_0\hat z$ is given by
\[\begin{pmatrix}S-\eta^2&-iD&0\\iD&S-\eta^2&0\\0&0&P\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}E_x\\E_y\\E_z\end{pmatrix}=0,\]
where $S=1-\dfrac{X}{1-Y^2},\ D=-\dfrac{XY}{1-Y^2},\ P=1-X$ with $Y=\omega_{cc}/\omega,\ X=\omega_{pc}^{\,2}/\omega^2.$\par
Obtain the expressions for $\eta$ for RCP and LCP wave modes. Discuss the polarization of these two modes.

Define ordinary (O) and extraordinary (X) waves for the propagation of EM waves perpendicular to the constant magnetic field $B_0\hat z$. Hence obtain the reflection and resonance points for these waves.
Write short notes on (i) Atmospheric whistlers (ii) Faraday rotation.

Consider the propagation of waves in a fully ionized warm plasma composed of electrons and singly charged positive ions with no external magnetic field. Show that the dispersion relation for longitudinal waves can be written as
\[\left(\omega^2-\omega_{pe}^{\,2}-k^2C_{se}^{\,2}\right)\left(\omega^2-\omega_{pi}^{\,2}-k^2C_{si}^{\,2}\right)-\omega_{pe}^{\,2}\omega_{pi}^{\,2}=0\,.\]
Hence obtain the Bohm-Gross dispersion relation. Discuss the cases of high-frequency and low-frequency oscillations. 
\par\hfill P.T.O.

\begin{center}[ 2 ]\end{center}
Explain what is meant by the term pinch effect in the confinement of a plasma by a magnetic field. Discuss the phenomena of Bennett pinch.
What is plasma sheath? Estimate the electric potential on the wall after the formation of the plasma sheath.
Prove that every regular space having countable locally finite base is normal.
State and prove Nagata-Smirnov metrization theorem.

Let $(X,U)$ be a uniform space and $D$ be the family of all pseudometrics on $X$ which are uniformly continuous from $(X\times X,\,U\times U)$ to $(\mathbb R,\,U_{\mathbb R})$ ($U_{\mathbb R}$ is the usual uniformity on $\mathbb R$). Prove that $D$ generates $U$.

Let $U$ be the uniformity generated by a family $D$ of pseudometrics on a set $X$. For each $d\in D$, let $U_d$ be the uniformity induced by the pseudometric $d$ and $Y=\prod_{d\in D}(X_d,U_d),\ X_d=X,\ \forall d\in D$. Prove that the evaluation mapping $f:X\to Y$ defined by $(f(x))(d)=x,\ \forall d\in D,\ x\in X$, is a uniform embedding.
Prove that a topological space is uniformizable iff it is completely regular.
Prove that a convergent net in a uniform space is Cauchy. Is the converse true? Answer with reasons. Prove that a Cauchy net is convergent iff it has a cluster point.
Prove that a uniform space is compact iff it is complete and totally bounded.
Prove that every continuous function from a compact uniform space to a uniform space is uniformly continuous.
Give an example of a topological group.
If $H$ is an algebraic subgroup of a topological group $G$ then show that $\bar H$ is also a subgroup of $G$. Also show that every open subgroup is a clopen subgroup.
Prove that in a topological group every component containing the identity element is a closed normal subgroup.

Let $(G,\tau)$ be a topological group and $H$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then prove that $\left(G/H,\tau'\right)$ is a topological group where $\tau'$ is the quotient topology induced by the canonical mapping $\phi:G\to G/H,\ \phi(x)=xH,\ x\in G$. Also show that $\phi$ is an open homomorphism from $(G,\tau)$ to $\left(G/H,\tau'\right)$.

Let $\alpha$ be an algebraic homomorphism from a topological group $(G_1,\tau_1)$ into a topological group $(G_2,\tau_2)$ and let $H$ be the kernel of $\alpha$. Further let $\alpha=\alpha_0\circ\phi$ for some $\alpha_0:G/H\to G_2$, where $\phi:G_1\to G_1/H$ is the canonical mapping. Prove that $\alpha:(G_1,\tau_1)\to(G_2,\tau_2)$ is continuous or open iff $\alpha_0:\left(G_1/H,\tau'\right)\to(G_2,\tau_2)$ is continuous or open ($\tau'$ is the quotient topology on $G_1/H$). Hence show that if $\alpha:(G_1,\tau_1)\to(G_2,\tau_2)$ is open homomorphism then the topological group $\left(G/H,\tau'\right)$ is isomorphic to $(G_2,\tau_2)$.
Prove that every locally compact Hausdorff topological group is normal.

Answer \underline{any two} : \par
\hspace*{1em}(i)\enspace Give an example of a $2^{\text{nd}}$ countable space which is not metrizable.\par
\hspace*{1em}(ii)\enspace Show that if a topological group is $T_0$ then it is $T_3$.\par
\hspace*{1em}(iii)\enspace Prove that a topological group is homogeneous.
Prove that a right $R$-module $M$ is Noetherian iff every submodule of $M$ is finitely generated.

Let $O\longrightarrow M_1\xrightarrow{\ f\ }M\xrightarrow{\ g\ }M_2\longrightarrow O$ be a short exact sequence of right $R$-modules and $R$-morphisms. Prove that $M$ is Artinian iff both $M_1$ and $M_2$ are Artinian.
Let $R$ be a right Artinian ring and $a,b\in R$ be such that $ab=1$. Then show that $ba=1$.

Define injective right $R$-modules. Prove that a right $R$-module $M$ is injective iff for every right $R$-module $N$, and submodule $N'$ of $N$, every $R$-morphism $f:N'\to M$ can be extended to an $R$-morphism $g:N\to M$.
Show that external direct sum $\displaystyle\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Delta}M_\alpha$ of $R$-divisible modules is $R$-divisible.
Prove that every $R$-module can be embedded into an injective right $R$-module.
Prove that every free module is projective. Is the converse true? Justify.
Prove that a right $R$-module $M$ is projective iff $M$ is isomorphic to a direct summand of a free $R$-module.
Let $M$ be a projective right $R$-module. Prove that the functor $Hom(M,-):Mod_R\to Ab$ is an exact functor.
Show that $J(R)=\{a\in R\mid 1+\mathrm{ras}\text{ is a unit for every }r,s\in R\}.$
Show that $M_n(D)$ is $J$-semisimple, where $D$ is a division ring.
Prove that a ring $R$ is semiprime iff it is a subdirect product of prime rings.
Prove that every ring is a subdirect product of subdirectly irreducible rings.
Show that every Boolean ring is a subdirect product of copies of the field $\mathbb Z_2$.

Let $R$ be a right semisimple ring. Prove that $R$ is a direct sum of finitely many minimal right ideals. Hence or otherwise show that every right semisimple ring is both right Artinian and right Noetherian.
Prove that a ring $R$ is right semisimple iff every right $R$-module is semisimple.
Let $M=\displaystyle\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}M_i$ where each $M_i$ is a simple right $R$-module and $M_i\simeq L$ for some simple right $R$-module $L$. Prove that $End_R(M)\simeq M_n\left(End_R(L)\right)$.
Prove that every closed convex subset of a Hilbert space $H$ has a unique member of smallest norm.
Show that a Hilbert space $H$ contains a complete orthonormal sequence iff $H$ is separable.
Let $M\subset H$ where $H$ is a Hilbert space. Prove that $M^{\perp}$ (orthogonal complement of $M$) is a closed subspace of $H$.

Let $f$ be a sesquilinear form defined on a Hilbert space and $\hat f$ be the associated quadratic form of $f$. Prove that $f$ is bounded iff $\hat f$ is bounded and moreover $\|\hat f\|\le\|f\|\le2\|\hat f\|$.
Prove that for every bounded linear operator $T:H\to H$ where $H$ is a Hilbert space its adjoint operator $T^*$ exists satisfying $\|T\|=\|T^*\|$.
Show that the collection of all self-adjoint operators defined on a real Hilbert space $H$ form a closed subspace of $B(H,H)$ where $B(H,H)$ is the set of all bounded linear operators defined on $H$.
If $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal operators defined on a Hilbert space $H$ such that either commutes with the adjoint of the other. Prove that $N_1+N_2$ and $N_1N_2$ are normal operators on $H$.

Let $T:H\to H$ be a self-adjoint operator where $H$ is a Hilbert space. Show that
\[\|T\|=\sup\{|\langle Tx,x\rangle|:\|x\|=1\}.\]
Prove that every self-adjoint operator is normal but converse may not be true.
Show that the spectrum $\sigma(T)$ of a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Banach space $X$ is compact (assume $\sigma(T)\neq\phi$).
Prove that residual spectrum $\sigma_r(T)$ of a bounded self-adjoint linear operator $T:H\to H$ (where $H$ is a complex Hilbert space) is empty.
Let $T\in B(H,H)$ where $H$ is a Hilbert space. Then prove that $\sigma(T^*)=\{k\in C:\bar k\in\sigma(T)\}$, symbols bear their usual meaning.
Let $A$ be a complex Banach algebra with identity. Show that for any $x\in A$, the spectrum $\sigma(x)\neq\varphi$.

Prove that spectral radius $r_\sigma(T)$ of a bounded linear operator $T$ defined on a complex Banach space can be expressed as
\[r_\sigma(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{\|T^n\|}.\]
Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be two projection operators on a Hilbert space $H$. Prove that $P_1+P_2$ is a projection operator on $H$ iff $P_1(H)$ and $P_2(H)$ are orthogonal.
Show that every unitary operator on a Hilbert space is isometric but not conversely.
Define $\sigma$- algebra? Give an example of a nontrivial $\sigma$- algebra.

Let $(X,\ \mathcal A,\ \mu)$ be a measure space. If $A,B\in\mathcal A,$ with $B\subset A,$ show that\par
\hspace*{1em}i) $\mu(B)\le\mu(A)$\par
\hspace*{1em}ii) if $\mu(B)<\infty$ then $\mu(A-B)=\mu(A)-\mu(B)$
When is a sequence of sets called convergent? Prove that a monotone increasing sequence of sets is convergent and converges to its supremum.

Consider the measure space $(\mathbb N,\mathcal P(\mathbb N),\mu)$ where $\mu$ is counting measure. Let $A_n=\{n,\,n+1,\,n+2,\ldots\}$. Show that $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\mu(A_n)\neq\mu\left(\bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty}A_n\right).$

Let $\mu^*$ be an outer measure on a set $X$. Let $\mathcal M$ be the class of all $\mu^*$- measurable sets. Show that $\mathcal M$ is an $\sigma$- algebra and $\mu^*$- restricted to $\mathcal M$ is a measure.

When is an outer measure $\mu^*$ on $X$ said to be regular? Let $\mu^*$ be a regular outer measure on $X$ and let $\mu^*(X)<\infty$. Prove that a necessary and sufficient condition that a set $A\subset X$ be measurable is $\mu^*(X)=\mu^*(A)+\mu^*(X-A)$.
Show that there is an outer measure on $\mathbb R^2$, constructed from premeasure such that under which open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ need not be measurable.

When is a measure $(X,\ \mathcal M,\ \mu)$ said to be complete? Show that there is a complete measure space $(X,\ \bar{\mathcal M},\ \bar\mu)$ such that $\mathcal M\subset\bar{\mathcal M}$ and $\bar\mu$ is extension of $\mu$ on $\bar{\mathcal M}.$
Show that the Lebesgue measure is complete.
What is simple function. If $f$ is nonnegative measurable function then show that there is a sequence of nondecreasing simple function which converges to $f$.
Show that sum and product of two simple functions are simple.
If $f$ is integrable on $E$ and $F\subset E,$ then show that $f$ is integrable on $F$. Moreover if $f$ is nonnegative on $E$ then show that $\displaystyle\int_F f\le\int_E f.$
If $f$ is integrable on $E$ and $c$ is constant, show that $cf$ is integrable on $E$ and $\displaystyle\int_E cf=c\int_E f.$
If $f$ be an integrable function defined on a measure space $(X,\ \mathcal M,\ \mu)$ such that $\displaystyle\int_E f\,d\mu=0$ for every $E\in\mathcal M,$ then show that $f=0$ a.e in $X$.

Let $(X,\ \mathcal M,\ \mu)$ be a measure space and let $E\in\mathcal M.$ If $\{f_n\}$ and $\{g_n\}$ be sequences of finite a.e, measurable functions on $E$ such that $f_n\to f\,[\mathrm{meas}]$ and $g_n\to g\,[\mathrm{meas}]$ on $E$, show that $f_n+g_n\to f+g\,[\mathrm{meas}]$ on $E$.
If $\mu(\mathrm E)=0$ then show that for any measurable function $f,\ \displaystyle\int_E f=0.$
Use tanh method to obtain the soliton solution of modified KdV equation and ZK equation.

Explain a classical plasma model of your choice. Write down the fluid equations. Find the group velocity and phase velocity of the linear wave after proper normalization and linearization of the equations.

Write down Sagdeev's equation for a plasma model. Compare Sagdeev's equation with Newton's potential equation. Explain the conditions for existence of soliton and double layer for Sagdeev's technique.

Write down an classical plasma model where ions are mobile and electron obey non-thermal distribution. Use RPT to obtain the cylindrical KdV equation. Obtain the soliton solution in absence of nonplanar term.
Starting from fluid equations to obtain the Burger equation of a plasma model of your choice by using a suitable perturbation technique. Obtain travelling wave solution.

Find the Sagdeev's Pseudopotential of an $e$--$i$ plasma where ions are mobile and electrons obey K distribution. Show that the shape of the exact solution may be obtained from the relation
\[\int_{\varphi_0}^{\varphi}\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{-2\psi(\varphi)}}=\pm\xi.\]
Obtain the soliton solution in small amplitude limit.

Prove that $A^i{}_{,i}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt g}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\left(\sqrt g A^k\right)$, where $g=|g_{ij}|$.\par
Hence prove that $\nabla^2\varphi=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt g}\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\left(\sqrt g g^{kj}\dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x^j}\right).$
Find the elementary arc length in cylindrical polar coordinate system.

Show that a necessary and sufficient condition that a vector field A with components $A^i$ is a parallel vector field along a curve $C$ given by $x^i=x^i(t),\ t_1\le t\le t_2,\ i=1,2,3$ is that $\dfrac{\delta A^i}{\delta t}=0$.
Using cylindrical polar coordinates prove that the curvature and torsion of the circle $x^1=a,\ x^2=\theta(s),\ x^3=0$ are $\dfrac1a$ and 0 respectively.
If the tangent and binormal to a space curve make angles $\theta$ and $\varphi$ with a fixed direction, show that $\dfrac{\kappa}{\tau}=-\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin\varphi}\dfrac{d\theta}{d\varphi}.$
If a Bertrand curve possesses more than one Bertrand associates, then show that it is a circular helix and in that case it possesses infinitely many associates.
Show that a twisted curve is a Bertrand curve if and only if its curvature and torsion are connected by a linear equation of the form $u\kappa+v\tau=1$, where $u,\ v$ are constants.
Show that parametric curves are geodesic if and only if $\left\{\begin{matrix}2\\11\end{matrix}\right\}=0=\left\{\begin{matrix}1\\22\end{matrix}\right\}.$
Show that geodesics are auto-parallel curves.
Prove that the unit tangent vector $t^\alpha=\dfrac{du^\alpha}{ds}$ of a geodesic $G$ is a parallel vector field along the geodesic.

Show that the catenoid
\[S_1:\ x^1=v^1\mathit{cos}v^2,\quad x^2=v^1\sin v^2,\quad x^3=a\cosh^{-1}\left(\frac{v^1}{a}\right)\]
obtained by revolving the catenary $x^2=\cosh\left(\frac{y^3}{a}\right)$ about the $x^3$-axis is isometric with the surface of the helicoid given by
\[S_2:\ x^1=u^1\cos u^2,\quad x^2=u^1\sin u^2,\quad x^3=au^2\]
where `$a$' is a constant and $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ are orthogonal cartesian coordinates.
What do you know about the relationship between regular simplex method and revised simplex method in connection with the finding of an optional solution to an LPP?

Given the following LPP:\par
Maximize $f(x_1,x_2)=3x_1+5x_2$\par
subject to \quad $x_1\le4$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_2\le6$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$3x_1+2x_2\le18$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2\ge0$.\par
\hspace*{1em}(i)\enspace Find an optimum solution to this programme by applying revised simplex method.\par
\hspace*{1em}(ii)\enspace Is the solution degenerate? Give reason for your answer.
State the economical use of the sensitivity analysis.

From the optimal simplex table of the following LPP\par
Maximize $f(x_1,x_2,x_3)=2x_1-x_2+3x_3$\par
subject to \quad $3x_1+x_2-2x_3\le6$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$2x_1+5x_2+x_3\le14$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1+4x_2+2x_3\le8$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$,\par
find the ranges of $C_2$ and $C_3$ such that the optimal basis remains unchanged.
Define pure and mixed integer linear programming problem (ILPP).

Solve the following all-integer programming problem using the `Gomory's cutting plane method'/`branch and bound method' :\par
Minimize $f(x_1,x_2)=3x_1+\frac52x_2$\par
subject to \quad $x_1+2x_2\ge20$,\par
\hspace*{4.2em}$3x_1+2x_2\ge50$,\par

Derive expressions for $\phi_{u_m}^{(1)x_i},\ i,m=1,2;\ \phi_{u_m}^{(2)x_ix_j},\ i,j,m=1,2$ in the prolongation of the infinitesimal generator $\hat X=\xi_i(\bar x,u)\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x_i}+\phi_{u_m}(\bar x,u_m)\dfrac{\partial}{\partial u_m}.$

A partial differential equation (PDE) $\dfrac{\partial^2u}{\partial x_{k_1}\partial x_{k_2}}(\bar x)=f\left(\bar x,u,\bar\partial u,\bar\partial^2u\right),(f(.)$ does not contain $\dfrac{\partial^2u}{\partial x_{k_1}\partial x_{k_2}}\Big)$ is linear, admits a Lie group of point transformations with infinitesimal generator $\hat X=\xi_i(\bar x,u)\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x_i}+\phi(\bar x,u)\dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}.$ Then show that $\xi_i(\bar x,u)$ are free from $u$ and $\phi(\bar x,u)$ is linear in $u$.

Verify whether the nonlinear wave equation $\dfrac{\partial^2u}{\partial t^2}=A^2(u+B)^4\dfrac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}$ admits a Lie group of point transformations generated by $\hat X=x^2\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}+x(u+B)\dfrac{\partial}{\partial u}.$ If yes, find similarity variables and reduced equation in terms of new variables.

Show that the KdV equation in one space dimension remains invariant under translations in space-time variables. Hence find corresponding group invariant solution which is localized in space (soliton).
Obtain the dispersion relation for stimulated Raman scattering in the nonlinear interaction of circularly polarized $EM$ waves with low-frequency electron plasma oscillations.
Explain the concepts of `phase velocity' and `group velocity' of a wave propagating in a conducting medium.
For the motion of an electron in an oscillating $EM$ field derive an expression for the ponderomotive force.

Consider the propagation of nonlinear wave packets in a dispersive plasma medium. Assuming a plane wave form of a perturbation, derive the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. Hence discuss the linear stability of its plane wave solution.

(i) Whistler waves, (ii) Helicons.

Starting from the Vlasov-Poisson system of equations obtain the dispersion relation for electron plasma oscillations. Hence explain the concept of two-stream instability in the wave-particle interaction.

Explain the concept of a kinetic Alfv\'en wave in plasmas. How is it different from the usual $MHD$ Alfv\'en wave? Show that the dispersion relation for kinetic Alfv\'en waves can be obtained as $\omega^2=\mathrm{k}_z^2\mathrm{V}_A^2\left(1+\mathrm{k}_x^2\rho_i^2\right),$\par

Define an orthonormal set in a Hilbert space $H$. If $\{e_k\}$ be an orthonormal sequence in $H$ then prove that for every $x\in H,\ \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|\langle x,e_k\rangle|^2\le\|x\|^2.$
Prove that every Hilbert space is reflexive.

When is an orthonormal set of vectors in a Hilbert space said to be complete? If $\{e_i\}$ be an orthonormal sequence in a Hilbert space $H$ then prove that for each $x\in H,\ x=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\langle x,e_i\rangle>e_i.$
Define sesquilinear form in a Hilbert space. Show that inner product in a Hilbert space is a bounded sesquilinear form.
State and prove Riesz representation theorem for a sesquilinear form in a Hilbert space.
If $T$ is a normal operator defined on a Hilbert space $H$, Show that $Tx=\lambda x$ iff $T^*x=\bar\lambda x\ \ \forall x\in H$ and $\forall\lambda.$
Defined unitary operator on a Hilbert space $H$. Prove that a bounded linear operator $T$ on $H$ is unitary if $T$ is surjective and isometric.
Prove that a continuous linear operator $T$ on a Hilbert space is unitary iff $\{T(e_i)\}$ is a complete orthonormal set whenever $\{e_i\}$ is a complete orthonormal set.
Prove that a continuous linear operator $T:H\to H$ where $H$ is a Hilbert space is normal iff $\|T^*x\|=\|Tx\|\ \ \forall x\in H.$
Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator defined on a Hilbert space. Show that $T$ is normal iff its red and imagenary parts commute.
Define Projection operator on a Hilbert space $H$ and show that a bounded linear operator $T:H\to H$ is a projection operator iff $T$ is self-adjoint and idempotent.

Let $T:H\to H$ be a bounded self-adjoint linear operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$. Show that a number $\lambda$ belongs to the resolvent set $\rho(T)$ of $T$ iff $\exists c>0$ such that for every $x\in H,\ \|T_\lambda x\|\ge c\|x\|.$
Prove that spectrum of a bounded linear operator on a complex Banach space is non-empty.

Define compact linear operator. Let $\{Tn\}$ be a sequence of compact linear operators defined on a normed linear space to a Banach space $Y$. If $\|Tn-T\|\to0$ then prove that $T$ is a compact linear operator where $\|\ \|$ is the norm on $B(X,Y)$.
Let $T:H\to H$ be a self-adjoint operator where $H$ is a complex Hilbert space. Show that eigen vectors corresponding to different eigen values of $T$ are orthogonal.
Define Banach algebra and give an example for the same.
Let $A$ be a complex Banach algebra with identity $e$. If $x\in A$ satisfies $\|x\|<1$ then prove that $e-x$ is invertible and $(e-x)^{-1}=e+\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}x^i.$

Let $W$ be the set of all self-adjoint operators defined on a Hilbert space $H$. For $T_1,T_2\in W$, define $T_1\le T_2$ if $\langle T_1x,x\rangle\le\langle T_2x,x\rangle\ \ \forall x\in H$. Prove that $\le$ is a partial order relation in $W$.
Give an example to show that the spectrum $\sigma(T)$ of a bounded linear operator on a real Banach space is empty.
State and prove Urysohn's metrization theorem. Give an example of a topological space which is not metrizable.

In a normal space $X$ if every closed set is an $G_\delta$-set then prove that for any open set $V,\exists$ a continuous function $f:X\to[0,1]$ such that $f(x)>0\ \forall x\in V$ and $f(x)=0,\ \forall x\in X\setminus V.$

Prove that the additive group of real numbers with usual topology is a topological group.

Prove that in a Hausdorff connected topological group every normal discrete subgroup is a closed normal subgroup of the centre.

Prove that if $f$ is meromorphic in the extended complex plane then it is a rational function.

Let $f(z)$ be meromorphic in $|z|<R$ and $f(0)\ne0$. Then show that $\log\left\{\left|\dfrac{\beta_1,\beta_2,\ldots\beta_n}{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots\alpha_m}f(0)\right|r^{m-n}\right\}=\dfrac1{2\pi}\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\log\left|f\left(re^{i\theta}\right)\right|d\theta.$

Let $b_1,b_2,\ldots b_n$ be the poles of $f(z)$ in $|z|<R$ and be analytic and non-zero else where inside and on $|z|=R$. Then show that if $z=re^{i\theta}\,(0\le r<R),\ f(z)\ne\infty$, then
\[\log\left|f\left(re^{i\theta}\right)\right|=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{R^2-r^2}{R^2-2rR\cos(\theta-\varphi)+r^2}\log\left|f\left(Re^{i\varphi}\right)\right|d\varphi+\sum_{\gamma=1}^{n}\log\left|\frac{R^2-\bar b_\gamma re^{i\theta}}{R\left(re^{i\theta}-b_\gamma\right)}\right|.\]
For any meromorphic function $f$ and finite complex constant `a', define $m(r,a),\ n(r,a),\ N(r,a).$
For any meromorphic function $f$ with $f(0)\ne0,\infty$, establish the formula $T(r,f)-T\left(r,\dfrac1f\right)=\log|f(0)|.$

If $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_p$ be $p$ meromorphic functions, then show that $T\left(r,\displaystyle\prod_{\gamma=1}^{p}f_\gamma\right)\le\displaystyle\sum_{\gamma=1}^{p}T(r,f_\gamma).$\par
Give an example to show sign of equality may occur for two meromorphic functions.
Show that $|T(r,f+a)-T(r,f-a)|\le2\log^+|a|+\log4,$ where `$a$'$(\ne\infty)$ is a complex constant.
Prove that for a meromorphic function $f,\ T(r,f)$ is an increasing convex function of $\log r$.

Let $S(r)$ be a real valued and non negative increasing function for $r_0<r<\infty$ and $r_0>0$. If $S(r)$ is of order $\rho\,(0<\rho<\infty)$ and has convergence class, then prove that $S(r)$ has minimal type. Does the converse hold? Support your answer.

State and Prove Nevanlinna's theorem on deficient values.

Define exact covariant functors. Show that the contravariant functor $Hom_R(-,M):Mod_R\to Ab$ is left exact.
Let $M$ be a right $R$-module. Show that the functor $Hom_R(-,M):Mod_R\to Ab$ is right exact if and only if $M$ is injective.

Let $M$ be a right $R$-module. Prove that $M$ is injective if and only if for every essential right ideal $A$ of $R$ and $R$-linear map $f:A\to M$, there is $m\in M$ such that $f(a)=ma$ for every $a\in A$.

Let $\{M_\alpha\}_\Delta$ be a family of right $R$-modules. Prove that $\displaystyle\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Delta}M_\alpha$ is projective if and only if $M_\alpha$ is projective for every $\alpha\in\Delta$.
Show that every $R$-module is a homomorphic image of a projective $R$-module.

Let $N$ be a submodule of $M$. Prove that $M$ is Noetherian if and only if both $N$ and $\dfrac MN$ are Noetherian.

Let $A$ be a right ideal of $R$. Prove that $A\subseteq J(R)$ if and only if for every right $R$-module $N\subseteq M$ with $\dfrac MN$ finitely generated, $N+MA=M$ implies that $M=N$.
Prove that a commutative ring $R$ is primitive if and only if it is a field.

Let $R$ be a ring. Prove that $P(R)=\{a\in R\mid a\text{ is strongly nilpotent}\}$.
Define radical $\sqrt I$ of an ideal $I$. Show that $\sqrt I$ is the intersection of all prime ideals containing $I$.
Show that an ideal $Q$ is semiprime if and only if $Q=\sqrt Q$.
Prove that a ring $R$ has a composition series if and only if it is both noetherian and artinian.
Define limsup and liminf for a sequence of sets $\{E_n\}$. Show that $\inf E_n\subset\liminf E_n\subset\limsup E_n\subset\sup E_n.$

What is completely additive set function? If $\psi$ is completely additive set function defined on a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal A$ and $\{E_n\}$ be a monotone increasing sequence in $\mathcal A$, then show that $\psi(\bigcup E_n)=\sum\psi(E_n).$
What is premeasure and covering family. Show that outer measure can be constructed from a premeasure.

Solve the following ODE by reducing into normal form, that is, the form where the first derivative is absent:
\[\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}-2x\frac{dy}{dx}+(x^2+2)y=e^{\frac12(x^2+2x)}.\]
(Unit I: Differential Equations II) (Full Marks: 40) Answer question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Let $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ be two independent solutions of the ODE
\[(1-x^2)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}-2x\frac{dy}{dx}+(2\cos^2x-1)y=0,\quad -1<x<1\]
with Wronskian $W(x)$. If $\left.y_1\right|_{x=0}=1$, $\left.\frac{dy_1}{dx}\right|_{x=0}=3$, $\left.y_2\right|_{x=0}=2$, $\left.\frac{dy_2}{dx}\right|_{x=0}=4$, find the value of $W(\frac12)$.
(Unit I: Differential Equations II) (Full Marks: 40) Answer question number 1 and any two from the rest.

Solve the ODE $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+(9-x)y=0$ in series near the ordinary point $x=0$. Hence find the particular solution for $\left.y\right|_{x=0}=\frac92$ and $\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=0}=\frac32$.

Find the particular solution of the following linear system using eigenvalue-eigenvector method:
\[\begin{aligned}
\frac{dx}{dt}&=4x+2y,\\
\frac{dy}{dt}&=3x-y,\\
x(t=0)&=77,\quad y(t=0)=49.
\end{aligned}\]

Solve the following simultaneous differential equations of type I:
\[\begin{aligned}
2\frac{dx}{dt}-\frac{dy}{dt}+2x+y&=11t,\\
2\frac{dx}{dt}+3\frac{dy}{dt}+5x-3y&=2.

Verify that the following total differential equation is integrable and hence solve the equation:

(Unit I: Differential Equations II) (Full Marks: 40) Answer question number 1 and any two from the rest.

A particle is let fall from rest from a point outside the earth at a distance $b$ from the centre. Prove that the square of the velocity of the particle on reaching the centre is $ga(3-\frac{2a}{b})$, where $a$ is the radius of the earth and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity at its surface.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
Define simple harmonic motion (SHM). Obtain the expressions for displacement, velocity, and acceleration of a particle executing SHM. Hence, derive expressions for its kinetic and potential energy.

Derive the equation of motion for a particle moving on a plane under the action of a force proportional to the distance of the particle from a fixed point on the plane.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
A particle moves freely in a parabolic path given by $y^2=4ax$, under a force always perpendicular to its axis. Find the law of force.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
Define central force and areal velocity.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
Derive the equation of motion of central orbit in polar coordinate system.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
State Kepler's laws of planetary motion. Show that the orbit is a conic section.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.
Find the law of force in the case in which a particle describes an orbid $r^2=2ap$ under a force to the pole.
Unit-II [Dynamics of a Particle (Full Marks: 40)] Answer any four questions.

Derive the equation of motion of a particle moving along a curve on a verticle plane under the action of gravity and a force of resistance that varies as the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ power of the velocity. A heavy particle is moving vertically upwards under the influence of a force of resistance proportional to the square of velocity. If the particle starts with an inital velocity $V$, find the maximum height it attains.
Prove that the sum of the reciprocals of the first $n$ triangular numbers is strictly smaller than 2.
Let $\{a_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence defined by $a_1=1$, $a_2=2$, $a_3=3$ and $a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}+a_{n-3}$ for all integer $n\ge4$. Prove that $a_n<2^n$ for every integer $n\ge1$.
Prove that 8 divides $5^{2n}+7$ for every integer $n\ge1$.
Prove that if an integer is simultaneously a square and a cube, then it is either of the form $7k$ or of the form $7k+1$ for some integer $k\ge1$.
Prove that the fraction $\frac{2n+1}{9n+4}$ is in its lowest term for every integer $n\ge1$.
Find all positive integers $n$ for which $(n+5)\mid(n^2+5)$.
Prove that $n^5+n^4+1$ is not a prime number for any integer $n\ge2$.
Prove that each positive integer of the form $3n+2$ has a prime factor of the same form.
If $p\ne5$ is an odd prime number, then prove that either $10\mid(p^2-1)$ or $10\mid(p^2+1)$.
If $p$ is a prime number, then prove that $\sqrt p$ is an irrational number.
Determine all positive integers $a,b$ and $c$ such that $\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c=1$.
Prove that a positive integer is divisible by 8 if and only if the integer formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_5\in\mathbb Z$ be such that $x_1^3+\cdots+x_5^3=0$. Prove that at least one $x_i$ is a multiple of 7.
Let $abc$ be a three digit positive integer. Prove that it is divisible by 7 if and only if 7 divides $(2a+3b+c)$.
Define the divisor function $\tau(n)$ and prove that if $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots p_k^{\alpha_k}$, where $p_i$'s are distinct prime numbers, then $\tau(n)=(1+\alpha_1)\cdots(1+\alpha_k)$.
Prove that $n$ is a perfect square if and only if $\tau(n)$ is odd.
If $f$ is a multiplicative arithmetic function, then prove that $g(n)=\sum_{d\mid n} f(d)$ is also a multiplicative arithmetic function.
Give an example to prove that $\sigma(n)$ is not completely multiplicative.
State and prove the M\"obius inversion formula.
Define the von-Mangdolt function $\Lambda(n)$ and prove that $\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)=\log n$.
Define the Liouville's function $\lambda(n)$ and prove that it is multiplicative.
Determine $\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\lambda(d)$ as a function of $n$.
Determine the number of zeros at the end of $100!$.
Prove that $\phi(n)\tau(n)\ge n$ for all integers $n\ge1$.
For any two integers $n\ge2$ and $k\ge1$, prove that the last digits of $n$ and $n^{4k+1}$ are same.
If $m\ge3$ and $n\ge3$ are two integers with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then prove that $U_{mn}$ is not cyclic.
Prove that every odd prime divisor of $9^n+1$ is of the form $4k+1$ for some integer $k\ge1$.
Find the area in the first quadrant included between the parabola $x^2=4y$, the $y$-axis and the line $y=25$.

Find the value of $\lambda(2)-\mu(2,1)$, where the tripple integral over the region bounded by the planes $2x+y+z=4$, $x=0$, $y=0$ and $z=0$ is given by $\int_0^2\int_0^{\lambda(x)}\int_0^{\mu(x,y)}dz\,dy\,dx$.
Change the order of the integration in the integral $\int_0^{\pi/2}dx\int_0^{\cos x}x^2dy$.
Find the condition for which the improper integral $\int_5^\infty x^\mu dx$ is convergent.
Find the value of the integration $\int_0^1 x^4(1-x)^3dx$.
Find the value of $y(\pi)$, where $y(x)=\frac{d}{dx}\int_{\sin^2 x}^{2\sin x}e^{t^2}dt$.
Is the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}x\sin\frac{\pi}{x};&x\in(0,1]\\0;&x=0\end{cases}$, a function of bounded variation on $[0,1]$.
Give an example of a bounded function for which lower and upper integral for a partition may not be equal. Justify your answer.
Use Second mean value theorem to show that $\left|\int_a^b\frac{\sin x}{x}dx\right|<\frac4a$.
Define $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ by $f(x)\begin{cases}1/x&\text{if }x>0\\1&\text{if }x=0.\end{cases}$ Examine if $(R)\int_0^1 f\,dx$ exists.
Give an example to show that the Riemann integral of a discontinuous function need not exist. Justify your answer.

By using the transformation $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, show that
\[\iint_E\frac{dx\,dy}{(1+x^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right),\]
where $E$ is the triangle with vertices at $(0,0)$, $(2,0)$ and $(1,\sqrt3)$.

If $f(x,\alpha)$ and $\frac{\partial f}{\partial\alpha}(x,\alpha)$ are continuous functions of $x$ and $\alpha$ for $a\le x\le b$, $c\le\alpha\le d$, $a,b$ being independent of $\alpha$, then prove that
\[\frac{d}{d\alpha}\int_a^b f(x,\alpha)dx=\int_a^b\frac{\partial f}{\partial\alpha}(x,\alpha)dx.\]
Using the above result, evaluate $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{(a^2\cos^2x+b^2\sin^2x)^2}$.
Prove that $\iiint_V(lx+my+nz)^2dx\,dy\,dz=\frac{4\pi}{15}(l^2+m^2+n^2)$, where $V$ is taken throughout the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=1$.
Applying Dirichlet's test, show that $\int_0^\infty\cos(x^2)dx$ is convergent.
Express $\int_0^1 x^m(1-x^n)^pdx$ as a Beta function and $\int_0^1\frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^n}}$ as a Gamma function.

Let $\alpha$ be a monotonic increasing function on $[a,b]$ and is continuous at $c$ where $a\le c\le b$. Let $f$ be a function be such that $f(c)=1$, and $f(x)=0$ for $x\ne c$. Prove that $f$ is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable and (RS) $\int_a^b f\,d\alpha=0$.
A function $f$ is bounded and integrable over $[a,b]$. If $\int_a^b[f(x)]^2dx=0$, then prove that $f(x)=0$ at all points of continuity of $f$.
If $f$ is Riemann integrable over $[a,b]$ and continuous at $c$, $a<c<b$, then prove that $\int_a^x f(t)dt$; $a\le x\le b$, is differentiable at $x=c$.
Show that the function $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2\cos\frac1x;&\text{if }x\ne0\\0;&\text{if }x=0,\end{cases}$ is a function of bounded variation on $[0,1]$.
Show that if $f(x)$ be monotone on $[a,b]$, $\int_a^b fdx$ lies in between $f(a)(b-a)$ and $f(b)(b-a)$.
Let $f(x)$ be Riemann integrable and nonnegative on $[a,b]$. If $f(x)$ be continuous at $c$ on $[a,b]$ and $f(c)>0$, then prove that $\int_a^b f(x)dx>0$.
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x&\text{if }x\ne\frac1n\\1&\text{if }x=\frac1n;\quad\text{for }n=1,2,\ldots.\end{cases}$ Is $f$ Riemann integrable on $[0,1]$? Give reasons.

A company manufactures two products of type I and type II. Processing of these products is done on two machines A and B. Type I product requires 2 hours per unit on machine A and 6 hours per unit on machine B. Type II product requires 5 hours per unit on machine A and no time on machine B. There are 16 hours of time per day available on machine A and 20 hours on machine B. Profit gained by the manufacturer from the product of type I and type II is Rs. 10 and Rs. 50 respectively. Solve the problem graphically to find the daily production of each of the two products in order to get the maximum profit.

Justify the statement: The dual of a dual problem is the primal problem. Apply the principal of duality to solve the LPP
\[\begin{aligned}
\text{Maximize }f(x_1,x_2)&=3x_1+4x_2\\
\text{subject to }x_1+x_2&\le10,\\2x_1+3x_2&\le18,\\x_1&\le8,\\x_2&\le6,\\x_1,x_2&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\]
Prove that the convex polyhedron is a convex set. Justify, whether the following set is convex and convex polyhedron: $X=\{(x_1,x_2)\mid x_1^2+x_2^2\le1\}$.
Give an example that the union of two convex sets may not be a convex set.

What is the relation between BFS and extreme point solution of a convex set of the feasible solutions of a given LPP? Find the extreme point solution for the equations,
\[\begin{aligned}2x_1+6x_2+2x_3&=3,\\6x_1+4x_2+4x_3&=2,\\x_1,x_2,x_3&\ge0.\end{aligned}\]

Prove that $x_1=2$, $x_2=3$, $x_3=0$ is a feasible solution but not a basic feasible solution of the set of equations
\[\begin{aligned}3x_1+5x_2-7x_3&=21,\\6x_1+10x_2+3x_3&=42.\end{aligned}\]
Reduce the feasible solution to a basic feasible solution and show that the solution is degenerate.

Solve the following LPP by simplex method:
\[\begin{aligned}\text{Maximize }f(x_1,x_2)&=2x_1+5x_2\\
\text{subject to }x_1+2x_2&\le8,\\x_1&\le4,\\0\le x_2&\le3\end{aligned}\]
and $x_1$ is unrestricted in sign. Is the solution unique? Justify your answer.

Solve the following system of linear simultaneous equations using the concept of LPP:
\[3x_1+x_2=7,\qquad x_1+x_2=3.\]

How can you detect that in a transportation problem the solution is optimal? What is the criterion for the existence of multiple optimal solutions? Solve the following balanced transportation problem by using VAM to determine the initial BFS: 
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr|r}
 &D_1&D_2&D_3&D_4&a_i\\\hline
 O_1&9&8&5&7&12\\
 O_2&4&6&8&7&14\\
 O_3&5&8&9&5&16\\\hline
 b_j&8&18&13&3&
\end{array}
\]

Under what conditions dual simplex method could be applied? Use dual simplex method to solve the following LPP:
\[\begin{aligned}\text{Maximize }f(x_1,x_2,x_3)&=-2x_1-x_3\\
\text{subject to }x_1+x_2-x_3&\ge5,\\x_1-2x_2+4x_3&\ge8,\\x_1,x_2,x_3&\ge0.\end{aligned}\]

Find the optimal assignment to find the minimum cost for the assignment problem with the cost matrix given by: 
\[
\begin{array}{cc|rrrr}
 &&\multicolumn{4}{c}{\text{Machines}}\\
 &&M_1&M_2&M_3&M_4\\\hline
 &J_1&10&24&30&15\\
 \text{Jobs}&J_2&16&22&28&12\\
 &J_3&12&20&32&10\\
 &J_4&9&26&34&16
\end{array}
\]

(i) Characterize the following terms in the context of game theory: Saddle point, Pure and mixed strategies. \par
(ii) Show that the $2\times2$ game $\begin{bmatrix}a_1&a_2\\a_3&a_4\end{bmatrix}$ is non-strictly determined, if $a_1>a_2$, $a_1>a_3$, $a_4>a_2$ and $a_4>a_3$.

(i) Show that the game problem $\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&-\beta\\-\gamma&\delta\end{bmatrix}$ is fair, if $\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma=0$. \par
(ii) Solve the following $2\times4$ game geometrically: 
\[
\begin{array}{ccrrrr}
 &&\multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{Player B}}\\
 &&B_1&B_2&B_3&B_4\\
 \textbf{Player A}&A_1&3&2&-1&4\\
 &A_2&2&5&6&-2
\end{array}
\]

Solve the game problem by reducing into $2\times2$ game problem using the dominance property
\[
\begin{bmatrix}0&0&0&0&0\\4&2&0&2&1\\4&3&1&3&2\\4&3&4&-1&2\end{bmatrix}
\]
Interpret the game result with optimal strategy.

If $P_1,P_2,\ldots,P_n$ be a given system of coplanar forces acting, respectively, at the points $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_n$ of a body, then show that the system of coplanar forces can be reduced to a single force $R$ at any base point $O$ and a single couple $G$.

A system of coplanar forces has the total moments $H$, $2H$ and $3H$ about the points $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$ and $(2,4)$ respectively. Find the magnitude and the equation of the line of action of the resultant.

(i) Define virtual displacement and virtual work for a rigid body acted upon by the force $F$. When a virtual displacement is said to be consistent with the geometrical conditions of the rigid body? \par
(ii) Find the virtual work done by the mutual action and reaction between two particles of a rigid body.

A solid hemisphere is supported by a string fixed to a point on its rim and to a point on a smooth vertical wall with which the curved surface of the hemisphere is in contact. If $\theta$ and $\phi$ are the inclinations of the string and the plane base of the hemisphere to the vertical respectively, prove that $\tan\phi=\frac38+\tan\theta$.

If a system of bodies be in equilibrium under the action of gravitational force only, discuss the conditions of its stability and instability. Hence, show that if the system has one degree of freedom, the stable and unstable positions of equilibrium occur alternatively.

A lamina in the form of a cycloid, whose generating circle is of radius $a$, rests on the top of another cycloid whose generating circle is of radius $b$, their vortices being in contact and their axes vertical. If $b$ \textit{[overwritten by handwritten $h$]} be the height of the c.g.\ of the upper cycloid above its vertex, show that the equilibrium is stable if $h<\frac{4ab}{a+b}$.

(i) Let a rigid body be subjected to the three external forces $X,Y,Z$, acting along the axes at $O$ with the resultant $R$ and a couple $G$ of moment $\sqrt{L^2+M^2+N^2}$. Prove that $R$ is invariant but not $G$. \par
(ii) If any three forces $P,Q$ and $R$, acting on a rigid body keep it in equilibrium, then show that they must be coplanar.

Six forces, each equal to $P$, act along the edge of a cube, taken in order, which do not meet a given diagonal. Show that their resultant is a couple of moment $2\sqrt3 Pa$, where $a$ is the edge of the cube.

Explain what is meant by Poinsot's central axis for a system of forces in three dimensions acting on a rigid body. \par
Hence define the terms Wrench, Pitch and Screw.
Two forces, act one along the line $y=0,z=0$ and the other along the line $x=0,z=c$. As the forces vary, show that the surface generated by the axis of their equivalent wrench is $(x^2+y^2)z=cy^2$.

Let a heavy particle of mass $m$ be compelled to move along a smooth cycloid, whose plane is vertical with its base $AB$ horizontal and vertex $O$ downwards. Discuss the motion of the particle on the cycloid. Hence determine the arc length from $O$ to any point $P$ in time $t$ on the cycloid and the reaction along the normal to the curve at $P$.

A smooth parabolic tube is placed, vertex downwards, in a vertical plane. A particle with weight $w$ slides down the tube from rest under the gravity. Prove that at any position, the reaction of the tube is $\frac{2w(h+a)}{\rho}$, where $\rho$ is the radius of curvature, $4a$ is the latus rectum of the parabola and $h$ is the original height of the particle above the vertex.
Find the area in the closed segment cut off from $y^2=4x$ by the line $y=2x$.
Test the convergence of the improper integral $\int_5^\infty\frac{dx}{x^\mu}$.
Find the value of the integration $\int_0^1 x^3\bigl(\log(\frac1x)\bigr)^5dx$.
Find the value of the integration $y(\pi)$, where $y(x)=\frac{d}{dx}\int_{\sin^2x}^{2\sin x}e^{t^2}dt$.

Find the differential equation corresponding to the integral equation
\[Y(x)=\int_0^x(x-t)Y(t)dt-x\int_0^1(1-t)Y(t)dt.\]
Using the properties of Riemann integral, show that if $f$ is a non-negative continuous function on $[0,1]$ and $\int_0^1 f(x)dx=0$, then $f(x)=0$ $\forall x\in[0,1]$.
Suppose $f(x)$ is a continuous real valued function. Then show that $\int_0^1 f(x)dx^2=\frac13 f(\xi)$ for some $\xi\in[0,1]$.

Show that there does not exist a primitive function on $\mathbb R$ to the function $f$ defined by
\[f(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\in\mathbb R^+\\0&x\in0\\-1&x\in\mathbb R^-\end{cases}\]
Give an example to show that the upper and lower integral (Riemann) may not be equal for a bounded function.
Is the function $f=\begin{cases}x\cos\frac{\pi}{2x},&x\ne0,\\0,&x=0,\end{cases}$ a function of bounded variation on $[0,1]$? Justify your answer.
Use the Second Mean Value Theorem (Bonnet's form) to show that $\big|\int_a^b\frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx\big|\le\frac2a$.
Let a function $f$ be Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$. Then show that $|f|$ is Riemann integrable. Give an example to show that converse of the result does not hold in general.
State and prove a condition for the Riemann integrability of $\frac1f$ for a Riemann integrable function $f$ on $[a,b]$.
State and prove the First Mean Value Theorem of integral calculus.
Let $f$ monotonic on $[a,b]$. If $\alpha$ is monotonic increasing and continuous on $[a,b]$, then show that $\zeta$ is Riemann-Stieltjes integrale on $[a,b]$.
Let $f$ be continuous on $[a,b]$, $f'$ exist and be bounded on $(a,b)$. Show that $f$ is a function of bounded variation on $[a,b]$.
Calculate total variation for the function $f(x)=x-[x]$, on $[1,3]$.

Find the value of $F(2,3,4)$, where
\[F(a,b,c)=\iiint_E\sqrt{a^2b^2c^2-b^2c^2x^2-c^2a^2y^2-a^2b^2z^2}\,dx\,dy\,dz,\]
$E$ being the region bounded by the ellipsoid $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}+\frac{z^2}{c^2}=1$.
Prove that $\int_0^1 dx\int_0^1\frac{x-y}{(x+y)^3}dy\ne\int_0^1dy\int_0^1\frac{x-y}{(x+y)^3}dx$. Does the double integral $\int_0^1\int_0^1\frac{x-y}{(x+y)^3}dxdy$ exist? Justify your answer.

Using the transformations $x=\frac12v(1-u)$, $y=\frac12v(1+u)$, evaluate the integral $\iint_E e^{\frac{y-x}{y+x}}dxdy$, where $E$ is the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Also verify the result by using the transformation $y-x=2u$ and $y+x=2v$.
Evaluate $\int_0^1dy\int_y^1 e^{x^2}dx$ by changing the order of the integration.
Evaluate $\iint_R[x+y]dxdy$, where $R$ is the rectangle $[-1,1;0,2]$ and $[x+y]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x+y$.
Express $\int_0^1x^m(1-x^n)^p$ in terms of Beta function. Hence evaluate $\int_0^1x^5(1-x^3)^{10}dx$.
Applying Dirichlet's test, show that $\int_0^\infty\sin(x^2)dx$ is convergent.

Peter wants to keep some hens with him and has Rs. 20000. The old hens can be bought for Rs. 300 but young ones cost Rs. 400. The old hens lay 20 eggs per week and the young ones 60 eggs per week, each worth being Rs. 5. The feed for young and old hens costs Rs. 100 and Rs. 60 per hen per week. He can keep 60 hens with him. How many of each kind of hens Peter should buy to get a profit of more than Rs. 5000. Formulate as an LPP.
Use simplex method to obtain the inverse of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\4&-1\end{pmatrix}$.

The two linearly independent equations with three variables are given below:
\[\begin{aligned}2x_1-3x_2+5x_3&=10,\\4x_1+x_2+10x_3&=20.\end{aligned}\]
Find, if possible, a basic solution with $x_2$, a non-basic variable.
Justify or correct the following statement: The objective function of an LPP assumes its optimal value at an extreme point of the convex set of feasible solutions.
Prove that the set $X=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1x_2\le2018,\ x_1\ge0,\ x_2\ge0\}$ is not a convex set.
State fundamental duality theorem of LPP. Why is it called fundamental?

Solve by Charne's Big M-method and prove that the following LPP has no feasible solution:
\[\begin{aligned}
\text{Maximize }z&=2x_1-x_2+5x_3\\
\text{subject to }x_1+2x_2+2x_3&\le2,\\
\tfrac52x_1+3x_2+4x_3&=12,\\4x_1+3x_2+2x_3&\ge24,\\
x_1,x_2,x_3&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\]

In a primal problem, the $5^{\mathrm{th}}$ constraint is an equation and the $4^{\mathrm{th}}$ variable is unrestricted in sign. What will be nature of the $5^{\mathrm{th}}$ dual variable and the $4^{\mathrm{th}}$ dual constraint? By solving the dual of the LPP
\[\begin{aligned}
\text{Minimize }z&=2x_1+2x_2\\
\text{subject to }2x_1+4x_2&\ge1,\\x_1+2x_2&\ge1,\\2x_1+x_2&\ge1,\\x_1,x_2&\ge0,
\end{aligned}\]
show that the optimal value of the primal as also of the dual is $\frac43$.

Solve the following LPP by two-phase method:
\[\begin{aligned}
\text{Minimize }z&=4x_1+x_2\\
\text{subject to }x_1+2x_2&\le3,\\4x_1+3x_2&\ge6,\\3x_1+x_2&=3,\\x_1,x_2&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\]

Use dual simplex method to solve the LPP:
\[\begin{aligned}
\text{Maximize }z&=-2x_1-3x_2-x_3\\
\text{subject to }2x_1+x_2+2x_3&\ge3,\\3x_1+2x_2+x_3&\ge4,\\x_1,x_2,x_3&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\]

Formulate the following transportation problem as an LPP:
\[\begin{array}{r|ccc|l}

In a transportation problem

&D_1&D_2&D_3\\\hline

Prove, analytically, that any system of coplanar forces acting on a rigid body will be in astatic equilibrium if $V=\sum_i(x_iX_i+y_iY_i)=0$ where $X_i,Y_i$ are the resolved parts of the forces $P_i$ acting at $(x_i,y_i)$ parallel to the coordinates axes $(i=1,2,\ldots,n)$.

A system of forces in one plane reduces to a couple whose moment is $G$. When each force is turned about its point of application through a right angle it reduces to a couple of moment $H$. Show that when each force is turned through an angle $\alpha$, the system is equivalent to a couple whose moment is $G\cos\alpha+H\sin\alpha$.
Use the principle of virtual work to find the conditions of equilibrium of a system of coplanar forces acting on a rigid body.

Define field of force, conservative field and potential energy of a system.

A body rests in equilibrium on another fixed body, being rough enough to prevent sliding. [Assume that the surface of the lower body, which is fixed, is convex upwards].
Find the conditions of equilibrium of a system of non-coplanar forces acting at different points of a rigid body.

Prove that, if equal forces act along the edges $BC,CA,AB,DA,DB,DC$ of a regular tetrahedron, the central axis is perpendicular from $D$ to the plane $ABC$ and the pitch of the equivalent wrench is $\frac{a}{2\sqrt2}$, where \textquoteleft a\textquoteright{} is an edge of the tetrahedron.
Prove that, whatever origin and axes are chosen, the quantities $LX+MY+NZ$ and $X^2+Y^2+Z^2$ are invariant for a given system of forces acting on a rigid body.
Forces $X,Y,Z$ act along the three straight lines $y=b,z=-c$; $z=c,x=-a$; $x=a,y=-b$ respectively; show that they will have a single resultant $\frac aX+\frac bY+\frac cZ=0$.

An open railway truck of mass $M$ is running on smooth horizontal rail under rain falling vertically which it catches and retains. A particle is allowed to slide down a smooth vertical circle of radius $27a$ from rest at the highest point. Show that, on leaving the circle, it moves in a parabola whose latus rectum is $16a$.
Evaluate the integral $\int_0^1 dx\int_x^{1/x}\frac{y\,dy}{(1+xy)^2(1+y^2)}$ by changing the order of the integration.
Evaluate $\iiint_V\frac{dx\,dy\,dz}{(1+x+y+z)^3}$, where $V$ is the tetrahedron bounded by the planes $x=0$, $y=0$, $z=0$ and $x+y+z=1$.
Evaluate $\iint_E\frac{dx\,dy}{\sqrt{(x+y+1)^2-4xy}}$, by using the transformation $x=u(1+v)$, $y=v(1+u)$, where $E$ is the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0)$ and $(2,2)$.

Let $f$ is a monotonic function on $[a,b]$, and $\alpha$ is a monotonic increasing function on $[a,b]$. If $\alpha$ is continuous then show that $f$ is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable on $[a,b]$.

Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded function and $P$ be a partition of $[a,b]$ with $\|P\|=\delta$. If $P_k$ be a refinement of $P$ with $k$ additional points, then show that
\[\begin{gathered}
U(P,f)\ge U(P_k,f),\ L(P,f)\le L(P_k,f);\ U(P_k,f)-U(P,f)\ge(m-M)kS,\\
L(P_k,f)-L(P,f)\le(M-m)k\delta,
\end{gathered}\]
where $m=\inf_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)$ and $M=\sup_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)$.

Show that if $f(x)$ be monotone on $[a,b]$ then $\int_a^b f(x)$ lies in between $f(a)(b-a)$ and $f(b)(b-a)$.
Let $f(x)$ be Riemann integrable and non negative on $[a,b]$. If $f(x)$ be continuous at $c$ on $[a,b]$ and $f(c)>0$, then prove that $\int_a^b f(x)dx>0$.

Prove that a countable union of countable set is countable.
(handwritten) If $A$ and $B$ are countable subsets of $\mathbb R$. Then prove that $A\times B$ is also countable.
Let $G$ be a group and let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be two subgroups of $G$. Prove that $H_1\cap H_2$ is a subgroup of $G$. Give an example to show that the result fails to hold for $H_1\cup H_2$.
Write the elements of the group $(\mathbb Z/12\mathbb Z)^*$. Is it a cyclic group? Justify your answer.
Give an example of an infinite group $G$ together with infinitely many distinct subgroups $H_1,H_2,\dots$ such that $H_1\subseteq H_2\subseteq\dots$. Justify your answer.
If by the rotation of axes, the expression $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c$ be changed to $a'x^2+2h'xy+b'y^2+2g'x+2f'y+c'$ then show that\\\centerline{(i) $a'+b'=a+b$ \qquad (ii) $a'b'-h'^2=ab-h^2$.}
What does the equation $x^2-3xy+3y^2+7x-18y+32=0$ become when the origin is moved to the point $(4,5)$ and axes are turned through an angle $45^\circ$.
The plane $x+2y+3z=6$ meets the co-ordinate axes in $A,B$ and $C$. Find the equation of the sphere $OABC$, $O$ being the origin and find out centre and radius of the sphere.
Prove, using vector method, that the quadrilateral formed by joining the midpoints of the consecutive sides of a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
State and prove the cosine law for triangles, using vector method.
Find the unit tangent $\vec T$, principal normal $\vec N$ and binormal $\vec B$ of the differentiable curve given by $\vec R(t)=3\cos t\,\hat i+3\sin t\,\hat j+4t\,\hat k$.
Let $A$ be a $4\times3$ matrix. If the three columns of $A$ are linearly independent then describe the reduced row echelon form of $A$.
Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix having columns $v_1,v_2,v_3$. If $v_2=2v_1+3v_3$, then determine the nature of solutions of $AX=0$.
Find a condition so that $\{(1,2,-1),(0,3,1),(h,k,t)\}$ is linearly dependent. Why is this condition restricts $(h,k,t)$ to be on a plane?
(i) Find $y_n$ when $y=e^x\cos x$\\(ii) Find $y_n$ when $y=\cos x\cos2x$.
Define monotone increasing sequence and give an example for the same. If a sequence is bounded above and monotone increasing then prove that it is convergent and converges to its Supremum.
State and prove Sandwich theorem and hence find the limit of the sequence $\{x_n\}$ where $x_n=\frac1{\sqrt{n^2+1}}+\frac1{\sqrt{n^2+2}}+\dots+\frac1{\sqrt{n^2+n}}$.
Let $\{u_n\}$ be a bounded sequence and $\lim_{n\to\infty}v_n=0$. Prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}u_nv_n=0$ and hence evaluate $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\sin n}n$.
Define reduced row echelon form of a matrix.
State a necessary and sufficient condition on the nature of solution of a linear system $Ax=b$.

Find solution(s) of either of the following systems. 
(i) $\begin{aligned}2x_1+x_2+x_3&=2\\x_1+x_2+x_3&=1\\x_1+x_2-2x_3&=3\end{aligned}$ \qquad (ii) $\begin{aligned}2x_2-x_3&=1\\4x_1-10x_2+3x_3&=5\\3x_1-3x_2&=6\end{aligned}$
Suppose a system of linear equations has a $3\times5$ augmented matrix whose fifth column is a pivot column. Is the system consistent?
Every row of the coefficient matrix of a system of three equations in three unknowns has a pivot position. Is the solution unique?
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $D,E$ and $F$ being the mid-points of the sides $BC,CA$ and $AB$, respectively. Prove that $\vec{AD}+\vec{BE}+\vec{CF}=\vec0$.
Determine a vector $\vec a$ such that $\vec a\times\hat j=\hat i-\vec c$.
If $\vec a,\vec b$ and $\vec c$ are three non-coplanar vectors, determine whether $\vec a\times\vec b,\vec b\times\vec c$ and $\vec c\times\vec a$ are also non-coplanar.

Find the angle by which the axes should be rotated so that the equation $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ becomes another equation in which the term $xy$ is absent. Hence find the angle through which the axes are to be rotated so that the equation $17x^2+18xy-7y^2=1$ may be reduced to the form $Ax^2+By^2=1$, $A>0$.
Find the equation of the sphere for which the circle $x^2+y^2+z^2=9$, $x-2y+2z=5$ is a great circle.
If by rotation of rectangular axes about the origin, $(ax+by)$ and $(cx+dy)$ be changed to $(a'x'+b'y')$ and $(c'x'+d'y')$ respectively then show that $ad-bc=a'd'-b'c'$.
The plane $x+2y+3z=6$ meets the co-ordinate axes at $A,B,C$. Find the equation of the sphere $OABC$, $O$ being the origin. Find the centre and radius of the sphere.

If $f$ and $g$ be two real-valued functions defined in some deleted neighbourhood of `c' and if $\underset{x\to c}{Lt}f(x)$, $\underset{x\to c}{Lt}g(x)$ exist and are equal to $\ell$ and $m(\neq0)$ respectively then prove that $\underset{x\to c}{Lt}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$ exists and is equal to $\frac{\ell}{m}$.
Using $(\varepsilon-\delta)$ definition, check whether $\underset{x\to0}{Lt}f(x)$ exists where $f(x)=$\\(i) $\cos x$; (ii) $\sin\frac1x$
Prove that every monotonic increasing sequence which is bounded above is convergent and converges to its supremum.
Check whether the sequence $\{x_n\}$, where $x_n=1+\frac1{1!}+\frac1{2!}+\frac1{3!}+\ldots+\frac1{n!}$, $n=1,2,\ldots,$ is convergent or not.

State Cauchy's $1^{st}$ limit theorem and use it to prove the following: if $\{x_n\}$ and $\{y_n\}$ converge to $x$ and $y$ respectively then $\{z_n\}$, where $z_n=\frac{x_1y_n+x_2y_{n-1}+\ldots+x_ny_1}{n}$, converges to $xy$.
Let $f(x)=x$ if $x$ is a rational number\\\hspace*{3.5em}$=1-x$ if $x$ is an irrational number\\Prove that $f$ is discontinuous at each real number except at $x=\frac12$.
State and prove Bolzano's theorem on continuous functions. Deduce that every continuous function $f:[a,b]\to[a,b]$ has a fixed point.
Show that the Supremum and Infimum of a non empty set $S$ are uniquely determined whenever they exist and that $\inf S\le\sup S$.
Prove that the greatest member of a set, if it exists, is the supremum of the set.
If $P_n=D^n(x^n\log x)$, then show that $P_n=nP_{n-1}+(n-1)!$\\Hence show that $P_n=n!\left(\log x+1+\frac12+\frac13+\ldots+\frac1n\right)$.

If $y=(x^2-1)^n$, then show that $(x^2-1)y_{n+2}+2xy_{n+1}-n(n+1)y_n=0$\\Hence show that if $z=D^n(x^2-1)$, then $z$ satisfies the following $2^{nd}$ order differential equation: $(1-x^2)\frac{d^2z}{dx^2}-2x\frac{dz}{dx}+n(n+1)z=0$.\\Write down the name of this type of the differential equation.
Adjust the constants $a$ and $b$ in order that $\lim_{\theta\to0}\frac{\theta(1+a\cos\theta)-b\sin\theta}{\theta^3}=1$.
State and prove Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem of Differential Calculus. Deduce Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem from Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem.
If $f$ is continuous in $a\le x\le b$ and $f'(x)>0$ in $a<x<b$, then show that $f$ is strictly increasing in $[a,b]$.
For any two sets $A$ and $B$, show that\\i) $A-B$ and $A\cap B$ are disjoint sets.\\ii) $(A-B)\cup B=A$ if and only if $B\subset A$.
Define a partial order relation.\\If $\rho$ be a relation on $\mathbb Z$ (set of integers) defined by $a\rho b\Leftrightarrow a-b$ is divisible by 5, then show that $\rho$ is an equivalence relation.
Give the definition of a mapping.\\If $X=\{2,3,4,6\}$ and $Y=\{2,4,6\}$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ be such that $f(2)=4$ and $f(3)=6$. Is $f$ a mapping? Justify your answer.

If a, b and c be the three sides of a triangle and s be the semiperimeter of the triangle, then show that $\begin{vmatrix}a^2&(s-a)^2&(s-a)^2\\(s-b)^2&b^2&(s-b)^2\\(s-c)^2&(s-c)^2&c^2\end{vmatrix}=2s^3(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)$.
If $A$ and $B$ be two invertible matrices of the same order, then show that $AB$ is invertible and $(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}$.
If $A$ be a real orthogonal matrix and $(I+A)$ be non singular, where I is the identity matrix then prove that the matrix $(I+A)^{-1}(I-A)$ is skew symmetric.
Show that an $n\times n$ matrix A is non-singular if and only if A is row equivalent to the identity matrix $I_n$.
Define a row reduced echelon matrix. Find the row reduced echelon matrix of\\$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\3&2&1\\1&-4&5\end{bmatrix}$ and hence find the rank of A.
Show that the equations $x+2y-z=3$, $3x-y+2z=1$, $2x-2y+3z=2$ and $x-y+z=-1$ are consistent and hence solve the equations.

If $(x_1+iy_1)(x_2+iy_2)\ldots(x_n+iy_n)=x+iy$, then show that\\i) $\tan^{-1}\frac{y_1}{x_1}+\tan^{-1}\frac{y_2}{x_2}+\ldots+\tan^{-1}\frac{y_n}{x_n}=\tan^{-1}\frac yx$ and\\ii) $(x_1^2+y_1^2)(x_2^2+y_2^2)\ldots(x_n^2+y_n^2)=x^2+y^2$.
Show that the product of all the values of $(1+i\sqrt3)^{3/4}$ is 8.
Show that the equation $(x-a)^3+(x-b)^3+(x-c)^3+(x-d)^3=0$, where a, b, c, and d are positive real numbers and not all equal, has only one real root.

If x, y and z be positive but unequal real numbers and $x+y+z=1$, then prove that $8xyz<(1-x)(1-y)(1-z)<\frac8{27}$.

Prove that the function $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$ is defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}x\sin\frac1x&;\ x\neq0\\0&;\ x\neq0\end{cases}$ is uniformly continuous.

State and prove Euler's theorem for a homogeneous function of two variables.

If $f(x,y)=x^2\tan^{-1}\frac yx-y^2\tan^{-1}\frac xy$ when $xy\neq0$ and $f(x,o)=f(0,y)=0$, then find $f_{xy}$ and $f_{yx}$ at $(0,0)$.
